under-deliver.

What we will not tell you **That it is definitely a carpenter ant.** Where the specimen is ambiguous we
will say so and get it looked at rather than picking the familiar answer.

title: Voles (Microtus spp.) in Whatcom County Lawns
sections:
Read the verdict first This profile exists because voles get confused with things we do handle, and
because the wrong diagnosis here sends people to the wrong trade and sometimes to
an unnecessary treatment. It does not exist to sell you anything.

What a vole actually is A vole is a small rodent built low and compact, and once you have seen one the
outline is hard to mistake.

The species that is actually here This matters because most vole content online is written about the meadow vole
of the eastern states or the California vole, and neither is what is in a
Bellingham lawn.
The runways are the diagnosis If you take one identification method from this page, take this one.

Vole, mole, or something else entirely This is where most of the confusion in this county sits, and the two animals
have almost nothing in common beyond living underground in a lawn.

What the damage looks like **Turf and ground cover.** Grazed patches, the runway network itself, and in a
bad year a lawn that looks scored and thinned across a large area once the grass
lifts in spring. UC IPM notes damage to turf and landscape plantings where the
dense vegetation they live in gives them cover.

Girdling, and why it all appears in one week The mechanism behind the worst of it is worth understanding because it explains
the timing, and the timing is what makes people think it happened overnight.

The cycle, and why some years are much worse Vole populations do not sit at a steady level and it is important to know that
before spending money on the assumption that this is now permanent.

Why this county suits them Nothing about vole pressure here is a reflection on how a property is kept. It
is a straightforward consequence of the climate and of how western Washington
landscaping is done.

What we do and do not do here Stated plainly, because the point of this page is to be useful rather than to
convert.

What actually works on voles None of this is a treatment, which is the whole point. Both extension sources
land in the same place.

What does not work **Rodenticide, for a homeowner in this state.** WSU states that no rodenticides
are registered for home use against voles in Washington. UC IPM notes that zinc
phosphide is the only toxicant usable against voles in residential settings in
California, which is a different state with different registrations, and it is
the kind of difference that catches people out when they read n

The one case that is ours There is a narrow exception and it is worth stating so nobody is caught by an
absolute.

Where to go instead For the horticultural side of this — which is most of it — the useful contacts
are the [WSU Extension](https://pubs.extension.wsu.edu/product/vole-management-in-home-backyards-and-gardens-home-garden-series/) Master Gardener program for Whatcom County, which handles
exactly this kind of question, and the extension publications listed below,
which are written for a homeowner rat

title: Webbing Clothes Moth (Tineola bisselliella)
sections: One fact explains the whole page Clothes moth larvae digest keratin. Everything else here follows from that.

It came in with something This is the honest framing for the whole fabric-and-pantry group, and it is worth
saying before anybody starts thinking about the building.

The adult, and why the moth at your lamp is not it The adult is small and unremarkable. UC IPM gives a wingspan of about half an
inch and a resting length of roughly a quarter inch, gold in color, with reddish
golden hairs on the top of the head and a row of golden hairs fringing the wings.
The Pacific Northwest handbook describes them as yellow or tan and about half an
inch across the wings. Kent

The larva does everything Kentucky describes the damaging stage as creamy-white caterpillars up to half an
inch long. UC IPM calls the larvae shiny white with dark colored head capsules.
Where the damage concentrates, and why Put the keratin rule together with the light rule and the map draws itself.

The Whatcom County version of the season Our climate changes the timing rather than the biology, and it changes it in one
direction: toward slower and longer.

Clothes moth or carpet beetle Both eat keratin, both damage the same items, and both feed in the dark. They are
separated by what they leave behind rather than by what they ate.

The other clothes moth, briefly There is a second species and it is worth being able to name, because the
evidence looks different enough to confuse somebody who has only read about the
first.
And it is definitely not the pantry moth The other confusion runs toward the kitchen, and one question settles it.

Heat, cold and laundering — the actual numbers Domestic tools work on this insect, and the figures are specific enough to be
worth writing down.
Mothballs and cedar, said honestly Both are trusted far beyond what they do.

Clean, then store — the entire prevention strategy If you take one action from this page, take this one, because it costs nothing
and it removes the conditions rather than the insects.
When treatment is warranted, and when it is not This species carries a verdict of *depends*, and it depends on two things.

What we will not do **Spray your wardrobe.** Garments are worn against skin and there is no version
of this problem where treating them is the right method.

What a result looks like on this species Development this slow makes progress genuinely hard to read, so it is worth
naming what counts as evidence and what does not.

Where to start Look for silk and tell us whether you found any, because that one observation
separates this species from the beetle and changes what the visit involves.

title: Western Black-Legged Tick in Whatcom County
sections:
We do not treat for ticks That is the verdict at the top of this page and it is worth putting in plain
words before anything else.

What the animal is *Ixodes pacificus* is a hard tick and an arachnid rather than an insect —
eight-legged as a nymph and adult, related to spiders and mites, as Washington
State University's veterinary hospital puts it.

Which tick you are looking at, and why it matters Washington's Department of Health illustrates four species that commonly bite
people here, and the distinctions are useful because the geography and the
diseases differ.

Where you actually meet one here Habitat is the most useful thing on this page after the removal instructions,
because it tells you when to do a tick check and when not to bother.

The season runs backwards from what you expect Most people carry a mental model of ticks as a hot-weather problem. For this
species that model is wrong in a way that matters locally.

The life cycle, which takes years *Ixodes pacificus* runs through egg, larva, nymph and adult, and takes a blood
meal from a different host at each of the three feeding stages. The whole cycle
occupies several years rather than a season, and each stage feeds once.

The honest version of the Lyme risk here This is the part of the page most worth reading carefully, because the public
conversation about Lyme runs to both extremes and neither is accurate for
Washington.

The other things carried here Washington's health department lists the tick-borne diseases known to be acquired
in this state: anaplasmosis, babesiosis, Lyme disease, Rocky Mountain spotted
fever, tick-borne relapsing fever, tick paralysis and tularemia.

Removing a tick, correctly Washington's Department of Health gives the method, and it is short enough that
there is no excuse for improvising.

What not to do, and why The folk remedies are not merely useless. Washington's health department warns
that hot matches, and coating the tick's body with petroleum jelly, soap or nail
polish, may cause it to release additional saliva, and that increases the chance
of transmitting disease.

What people bring us that is not a tick A fair share of the photographs we get sent under this heading are something
else, and the misidentifications run in a consistent set.

Recording a bite, and what to tell a doctor Because the diagnosis is clinical and the window matters, a small amount of
record keeping is worth more here than it is with most things in this library.
Prevention that is worth the effort The measures that reduce exposure are behavioral, and they are cheap.

Property, pets and what actually helps If your land includes a brushy margin, the honest advice is habitat rather than
chemistry. Keeping grass cut where people and animals walk, clearing leaf litter
away from the areas that get used, cutting back the vegetation that leans over a
path, and maintaining a clear separation between the mown area and the wooded edge
all reduce contact with the places t

Why this page exists at all A pest control company that will sell you a treatment for anything you are worried
about is not a company doing you a service. Ticks are the clearest example we
have.

title: Western Conifer Seed Bug — Large, Loud, Harmless
sections:
The thing that flew at the lamp It is a mild October evening, a reading light is on, and something roughly the
size of a thumb joint comes across the room with a buzz you can hear from the next
chair. It hits the shade, drops, rights itself, and sits there looking prehistoric.

Recognizing one **Size.** Large by household standards. Colorado State puts the adult at about
three quarters of an inch, and Montana State gives a range of roughly half to three
quarters — nine to eighteen millimeters. That is big enough to see clearly from
across a room, which is half the reason for the alarm.

What people call it instead Four misidentifications account for nearly every call, and it is worth taking them
in order of how frightening they are.
The conifers, and why that puts it on your wall The trees are why this animal is here in the numbers it is.
The year it has One generation, run on a simple schedule.
What it does indoors The honest list is short, and most of it is a list of things that do not happen.
The smell They do produce an odor, and it is the mildest of the three insects on the wall.

Why we say treating is rarely warranted The verdict at the top of this page is that treatment is rarely worth buying for
this species, and the reasoning is arithmetic rather than principle.

Where to seal The openings that matter are mostly above head height, which is why this keeps
happening on buildings where somebody has carefully sealed everything they could
reach from the ground.

Around this county **The forest edge.** Sudden Valley, Silver Beach, Edgemoor, Geneva, the whole Lake
Whatcom shore, and any property backing onto second growth. Conifers on three sides
and a warm south wall in the middle is the classic setup, and this species dominates
the autumn calls there.

Children, pets and the panic response Because this is the insect that makes people scream, it is worth being explicit
about how safe it is.

How many is a lot People ask us whether their numbers are normal, and it is a fair question because
nobody has a baseline for this.

What actually happens when we come out Since the honest answer for this species is usually that no treatment is warranted,
it is worth saying what a visit consists of instead.

What is not worth buying **Foggers and total-release products.** They do not reach a wall void, which is
where the insects are.

The short version Large, brown, narrow, with paddles on its back legs and a wingbeat you can hear.
It came out of the conifers, it wants to be somewhere warm until March, and it can
do you and your building no harm whatsoever.

title: Western Yellowjacket in Whatcom County
sections:
The wasp that ruins the end of summer Ask people in this county when wasps are bad and you will get the same six-week
window every time: the back half of August through the middle of September. That
is not an impression. It is arithmetic, and the western yellowjacket is the
species doing most of it.

The year, in one arc A colony is annual. It exists for about seven months and then it is gone, and
each stage explains something people notice.

Why late-season aggression is a food story This is the part worth understanding properly, because it explains the behavior
people find inexplicable — a wasp that ignored them in June landing on their
plate in September, and the same insect defending a hole in the lawn far harder
than it did two months earlier.

What it looks like, and what it is not Getting the species right changes the answer, and three insects account for
nearly all the confusion here.

Where the nests are Underground, overwhelmingly, and the site selection is consistent enough to
predict.

Nest location decides the job This is the practical heart of the page, and it is why the verdict at the top of
this profile is that it depends.

Finding the entrance without getting hurt If somebody has been stung on a lawn and nobody knows where it came from, the
entrance can be located safely from a distance.

When leaving it alone is the right call Not every ground nest is worth treating, and saying so is more useful than
selling every one.
What treatment involves Done properly, a ground nest is treated rather than dug out.

The things people try that go wrong There is a settled folk repertoire for ground nests and every item in it puts a
person directly over an angry colony at close range.

Stings, and when it stops being a pest control question Yellowjackets do not lose the sting the way a honey bee does, so one insect can
sting repeatedly, and a disturbed ground colony recruits.

The one indoors in November, and the one in February Two off-season sightings puzzle people every year, and both have the same
explanation.

Lowering the count next year A few habits genuinely reduce how many nests a property carries, and none of
them involves treating anything.

Around the county **Sudden Valley, Silver Beach and the lake margins.** Banks, root plates and
forest edge, on properties where people are outdoors in precisely the ground the
nests are in. The highest concentration of ground-nest calls we take.

Related work The county-wide picture, the other stinging species and how the season is worked
sit on [wasp and hornet control](/services/wasp-control/). For the specific
situations, [yellowjackets in the
lawn](/services/wasp-control/yellowjackets-in-the-lawn/) covers ground nests in
detail and [wasp nest in a wall
void](/services/wasp-control/wasp-nest-in-a-wall-void/) covers the structural
versio

title: Wood-Boring Weevil in Whatcom County
sections:
An insect this region actually has and nobody writes about There is a short list of wood-destroying organisms that turn up in Whatcom
County buildings, and one of them is almost entirely absent from the material
published about the Pacific Northwest. It gets found, it gets misidentified as
something else, and the misidentification quietly changes what happens next.

Where it came from, and why it likes it here This species is not native to North America. It is a New Zealand insect that has
traveled with timber and cargo: recorded in Great Britain in 1937, and in
Canada by around 1980.

Look at the head Everything about the identification comes down to one feature, and it is
unmistakable once you know to look.
The requirement that defines it Here is the fact that makes this species useful rather than merely unwelcome.
What the damage looks like Four features, and three of them separate it from the beetles.

Telling it from the anobiid, in order These two account for nearly all the small round-ish holes found in Whatcom
County structural timber, and running the checks in this order gets you there
fast.
Where it turns up in this county Follow the water to its worst point in the building and that is where to look.
Season and life cycle Slower than an insect this size suggests.
What the finding is actually worth Proportion matters here, and the honest framing is unusual for a pest page.

What the misidentification costs It is worth spelling out what goes wrong when this insect is written up as a
powderpost beetle, because the error is common and it is not harmless.
What to do before anybody comes out Four things, and they are the ones that make a visit worth having.

How urgent this is, honestly Somewhere between the two positions people arrive with, and closer to the calm
end than the marketing suggests.
What treatment involves, and what it depends on The verdict is *depends*, and the variable is not the insect.

What we will not sell you **A treatment over an unrepaired leak.** The wood will be wet again by February
and the fungi will still be working. Applying product to it changes the invoice
and not much else.
What you get in writing Stated plainly, because it is the point where this category gets slippery.

Related work Because the finding is a decay finding, most of the follow-through sits with
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/) and
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/). The insect is grouped
with the other timber borers on the
[wood-boring bee and beetle page](/services/carpenter-bee-control/), and the
wider structural picture is on
[termite

title: Yellow Sac Spider: The One That Does Bite
sections:
Why this one gets its own page Most of what this library has to say about spiders is that the frightening ones
are harmless. This page is the exception, and it is worth being straight about
in both directions.
What it looks like Small, pale, and unremarkable, which is most of why people do not spot them.
The silk pocket, which is the real field mark You are far more likely to find the retreat than the spider.

It hunts, and that is why it bites The behavior is the whole explanation for the medical entry, so it is worth
laying out plainly.
What a bite is actually like From the verified-bite literature rather than from the internet.

The necrosis story, and why the evidence does not support it This is the same correction this site makes about the hobo spider, applied to a
different species, and it comes from the same body of work.

When to see a doctor We are not qualified to give medical advice and this is not it. What we can do
is repeat what the state health department says and be clear about where our
competence stops.

Telling it from the big autumn spider Almost every spider call this county produces in September is a giant house
spider, and the two are not easily confused once you have a size in mind — but
people who have read about sac spiders start seeing them everywhere, so it is
worth a short list.
Where they turn up in this county The pattern is about vegetation outside and junctions inside.

The year, and the eggs The seasonal shape is less dramatic than the funnel weavers and it still has a
shape.
What actually reduces them Physical work, in this order, because the product does the least of it.
Our verdict, and where the line sits This one genuinely depends, and here is what it depends on.

What we will not tell you **That it causes flesh-destroying wounds.** Fifty-nine verified bites say
otherwise, and we would rather cite them than trade on the story.

Related work The large spider people actually meet in autumn is the
[giant house spider](/pest-library/giant-house-spider/), and the one carrying an
undeserved reputation is the [hobo spider](/pest-library/hobo-spider/). Our
general approach, including why spraying underperforms on spiders, is on
[spider control](/services/spider-control/). Sealing the gaps and getting the
planting off the walls i

title: Ant & Carpenter Ant Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
Three ants, and only one of them eats your house More money is wasted on ant treatment in this county than on any other pest,
and almost all of it comes down to one mistake: treating the ant you can see
instead of identifying which ant it is.

Odorous house ants **Odorous house ant** (*Tapinoma sessile*). Small, dark brown, and unmistakable
once you know it — crushed workers smell strongly of coconut or blue cheese.
Nests indoors and out, often in wall voids, under floors, or beneath objects on
the ground. The important thing about this species is the budding described
above: it is the ant that most often gets worse after somebody treat

Carpenter ants **What they are.** *Camponotus modoc* is the common one here — large, matte
black, workers ranging from about a quarter to over half an inch in the same
colony, because carpenter ants are polymorphic. That size variation is a useful
field mark. A single evenly-sized column of ants is probably not carpenter ants.

Moisture ants **What they are.** Several *Lasius* species, smaller than carpenter ants, and
usually yellowish to light brown rather than black. Some produce a distinctly
citrus or lemony smell when crushed.

The others you will meet here **Pavement ant.** Small, dark, characteristically nesting under slabs, driveways,
walkways and against foundations, throwing up small soil craters at cracks and
expansion joints. Mostly an outdoor nuisance that comes inside to forage.

Why the hardware-store approach usually fails Three reasons, and they are worth understanding because they explain most of
what people have already tried before calling us.

How we work an ant job **Identify.** Under magnification where it matters. Everything downstream
depends on this, and it takes minutes.

Around the county **Prewar Bellingham** — Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York, Roosevelt,
South Hill. Post-and-pier foundations, sill plates close to grade, and a century
of gutter and flashing history. This is moisture ant country, and the finding is
usually water rather than ants.

What the damage looks like over time Carpenter ants work slowly. A satellite colony is not going to bring a wall down
in a season, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency. What they do
over years is hollow structural members along the grain — sill plates, headers,
studs around windows, joists near a chronically damp area — and because they
prefer wood that is already slightly softened,

What it costs We quote from an inspection. A single accessible satellite colony in a door
frame is a small job. A house with a parent colony in the yard, two satellites in
the structure, and a moisture source feeding both is a larger one, and where the
finding is a failed gutter or a leaking supply line, part of the fix is
somebody else's trade.

The ant year in Whatcom County Ant activity here follows a predictable arc, and knowing where you are in it
tells you a lot about what you are looking at.

Commercial and multifamily ant work In apartments, condominiums and HOA-managed buildings, ants raise the same
structural problem bed bugs do: a colony does not respect unit boundaries. Wall
voids, utility chases and shared plumbing runs connect units, and treating one
apartment while the adjacent one goes untouched simply moves the nest.

Keeping them out Fix the water first — gutters, downspouts discharging away from the foundation,
crawlspace drainage and vapor barrier, and any plumbing you already know about.
Keep bark mulch and soil below the siding line. Move woodpiles off the ground and
away from the house. Take out stumps within reach of the property where you
reasonably can. Cut branches that touch the roof or walls, becaus

Related work Ant findings frequently open into
[exclusion and repair](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) work, and where the
moisture source is a crawlspace, into
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/). Wood
that is soft enough to host moisture ants is also worth checking for
[dampwood termites and other wood-destroying pests](/services/termite-control/),
which fol

title: Ant Trails Across the Kitchen Counter
sections:
The trail is the most useful thing in your kitchen A line of small ants moving in both directions across a counter, along the back
of a sink, or up the wall behind a kettle is one of the most common calls we
take, and the universal first reaction is to wipe it away or hit it with a
spray.

Why spraying it makes things worse The aerosol under the sink kills the ants it lands on. Everyone knows that part.
What is less well known is what it does to the rest of the population.

What they probably are The small ants that come into kitchens here fall into a handful of groups, and
the identification changes the treatment.

Why now Ant calls in this county follow the weather more closely than they follow
anything else.

The response that works **Identify first.** Species determines bait choice, and bait choice determines
whether this works. A sugar bait offered to a grease-feeding species sits
untouched.

Where the nest actually is People picture an anthill. In a residential setting here, the nest is usually
somewhere less obvious and there is a fairly consistent shortlist.

What makes a kitchen attractive Since the usual worry is that this reflects on the household, it is worth
setting out what actually counts as a resource from an ant's point of view.
Almost none of it is what people expect.
When it is not a nuisance ant at all Three findings change the conversation and are worth ruling out.

How long it should take Expectations are where most dissatisfaction with ant work comes from, so here is
the honest shape of it.

Ants outside, and when to leave them A last point that runs against the grain of this trade: most ants on your
property are doing no harm and are worth leaving alone.

Restaurants, cafés and food premises If the counter in question is commercial, the same biology applies but the
constraints do not.
What you get from us We follow the trail rather than treating the counter.

title: Carpenter Ants in a Window Frame
sections:
Why it is the window Carpenter ants around a window frame is one of the most frequent calls we take
in this county, and the reason is not really about ants at all. It is about
water.
What you are actually seeing The signs cluster in a few recognizable forms.

Satellite nests and the parent colony This is the concept that determines whether the work holds, so it is worth
setting out carefully.

Finding the parent colony On a modest city lot this is usually quick. There are a limited number of
candidates and they are all within sight of the house.

The moisture side of the job You can treat the ants perfectly and still be back here in three years if the
window stays wet, so the building work matters.

What the treatment actually involves Done properly, the work has several parts and none of them is a spray on a
windowsill.
Telling them apart from the alternatives Two things get confused with carpenter ants and both change the answer.

What people try first Nearly everybody does something before calling, and some of it actively makes
the job harder.

The species you actually have Two carpenter ants account for most of what we see in Whatcom County, and
knowing which one you have shifts where we look.

Windows differ by building age The buildings in this county fall into a few groups and each fails in its own
way.
What we will not sell you **A spray-and-go visit.** It treats what you can see and leaves the colony.

When to act Carpenter ant activity is most visible from spring through late summer, with a
noticeable peak as the weather warms and again in the swarm period. A single ant
in February in a heated house is more significant than a single ant in July,
because it suggests something is overwintering inside rather than wandering in.

What happens when you call We look at the window itself — the frame, the sill, the trim, the openings and
the frass. We look at the wall assembly around it and at where the water is
coming from. We walk the exterior and the grounds for the parent colony, in the
evening if that is what it takes to follow a trail.

title: Moisture Ants Mean a Water Problem
sections:
An ant that works as a diagnosis Most pest findings tell you that something got in. Moisture ants tell you
something quite specific about the building itself, and that makes them unusual
and, in an odd way, useful.
What they look like They are easy to mistake for other small ants until you know the tells.

Where the water usually is In this county, the places that produce moisture ant findings are consistent
enough to list.

The condensation cases Not every water problem is a leak, and the ones that are not tend to go
undiagnosed longest.

Why treating them first is the wrong order We treat moisture ants where it is warranted. We do not lead with it, and the
reason is simple arithmetic.

What the repair usually involves We are not builders and we do not quote building work. What we do is identify
precisely what is wet and why, so that the right trade is fixing the right
thing.

What else you tend to find alongside them A wet crawlspace or a wet wall cavity supports a whole community, and moisture
ants are usually not traveling alone.
Telling them apart from the alternatives Three things get confused with moisture ants and each changes the answer.

If they have just swarmed indoors A sudden emergence of small winged ants inside a room is the most common way
this problem introduces itself, and it is worth knowing what to do in the hour
it is happening.

Why this is a common finding here Whatcom County produces more of this than most places, and the reasons are
climatic and structural rather than anything to do with housekeeping.

When a sale is involved Moisture ants come up in property transactions more often than any other insect
we deal with here, because the places they occupy are exactly the places a
buyer's inspector looks.

What we will not sell you **A treatment as a substitute for a repair.** It does not work and it hides the
thing that matters.
What happens when you call We look for water before we look for ants.

title: Sawdust Piles Below the Trim — What It Means
sections:
It is almost certainly not sawdust Someone notices a small heap of pale wood-colored material on a floor, a
windowsill, a stair tread or the top of a baseboard. It looks like sawdust,
so that is what it gets called, and quite often it gets swept up and forgotten.

Look at the texture first Pick a small quantity up between finger and thumb, or better, put some on a
sheet of white paper where you can see it properly.

Then look at what is in it This is the step that resolves most remaining ambiguity, and it needs nothing
more than good light.
Where the pile sits The location narrows it further, because each of these has habits.

The four candidates in more detail **Carpenter ants.** The most common of the four here by a wide margin. They
excavate galleries to nest in and do not consume the wood. Galleries are
characteristically smooth, almost sanded, and kept clean, which is why the
debris ends up outside. Activity peaks in spring and summer, and it is strongly
associated with timber that has been wet. Critically, what is

What to do before anyone comes out Three things, none of which takes long, and all of which make the visit more
useful.

The openings tell you as much as the pile Once you have followed the debris upward, the shape of the hole it came out of
is its own identification.

When the trim itself is the problem Modern trim materials change this picture and it is worth knowing which you
have.

The crawlspace version of this finding Debris found on a crawlspace floor, on a vapor barrier or on concrete below a
beam is the same evidence in a more consequential location, and it deserves a
different level of attention.

What we will not sell you **A treatment before an identification.** If we cannot tell you what you have,
we are not going to quote you for treating it.

Why identification decides the price Homeowners sometimes find it strange that we will not quote from a description,
and it is because the four answers carry very different work.

Damage, in proportion People are usually more frightened by the pile than the situation warrants, and
occasionally less frightened than they should be, so here is the proportionate
view.
Seasonality, and what it adds When the debris appears is another piece of evidence, and it is free.

Bring us the pile The quickest route through this is to keep a sample, photograph the opening, and
have somebody look at the timber it came from.

title: Attic Insulation Removal & Replacement | Bellingham
sections:
Why this ends up being a pest page Attic insulation replacement sits on a pest control site for a simple reason:
almost every one we do follows an animal.

Contaminated, or just thin? Two genuinely different jobs, and the honest distinction matters because one of
them costs several times the other.

The order, again Same rule as the [crawlspace](/services/crawlspace-restoration/), and it is worth
repeating because getting it wrong is expensive.

What the work involves Two crews, one job, in this order. Ours does the pest side and the crawlspace;
the insulation contractor does the attic.

Air leaks, which we will point out and do not seal We do not offer air sealing. It is worth saying plainly, because a lot of
companies fold it into an insulation quote and it is the kind of thing a
homeowner assumes is included. It is not included here.

What you get for it **Comfort, quickly.** Most heat loss goes up, so upstairs rooms hold temperature
noticeably better. People report it within a week of cold weather.

How much insulation is right Whatcom County sits in a marine climate zone where the current recommendation for
attics is roughly **R-49 to R-60**.

Around the county **The century-old city housing.** Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York, Roosevelt and South Hill. Original or minimal insulation, decades of rodent access through
soffit and roofline gaps, and knob-and-tube era wiring that needs identifying
before anything is blown in. The largest efficiency gains in the county are in
these attics.

Where we hand off, and to whom We are a small local company and we would rather tell you the limits of that
than stretch past them.

What it costs Priced from the attic, driven by square footage, existing insulation type and
depth, contamination extent and access.
Timing Any time of year works, with two preferences.

What we find up there The attic is the least-visited part of most houses, and what turns up is
consistent enough to list.

Blown-in or batts? A reasonable question and the answer is mostly about the attic rather than the
material.
For landlords and property managers Two reasons this comes up outside owner-occupied homes.

Ventilation, which decides whether any of it works Insulation and ventilation are frequently treated as separate trades, and in an
attic they are the same conversation.
After the work Two habits keep an attic in the condition you just paid for.

Related work This work almost always follows [rodent control](/services/rodent-control/) or a wildlife specialist's removal work, and it belongs in the same project as
the [exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) that close the
entry points. Where the crawlspace is in similar condition — and on older homes
it usually is — see
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlsp

title: Bed Bug Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
Verification first, and why we charge for it Most pest companies will book a bed bug treatment off a phone call. We will not,
and the reason is that a meaningful share of the calls we get about bed bugs are
not bed bugs.

What treatment costs Treatment is **$395 per room**, and common areas are included rather than
counted as extra rooms. A one-bedroom apartment with an infested bedroom and a
living room the occupant has been sleeping in is not billed as two rooms plus a
hallway.
Why bites are the worst evidence This is the single most useful thing on this page, so it goes near the top.

What to actually look for **The insects.** Adults are about the size and shape of an apple seed, flat,
reddish-brown, and noticeably rounder and darker after feeding. Immatures are
smaller and much paler — nearly translucent when unfed, which is why people miss
them.

What gets mistaken for them **Carpet beetle larvae** are the most common false alarm — small, fuzzy, found
in bedding, and they cause skin irritation in some people that looks like bites.

How they get in Bed bugs are a **travel and furniture** problem. They do not come up from the
yard, they are not attracted by food waste, and they have nothing to do with
housekeeping. They arrive in luggage, in a backpack, on secondhand furniture, on
a guest, or through a shared wall.
The Bellingham pattern Two things about this market are worth knowing.

Preparation is most of the job This is where bed bug treatment succeeds or fails, and it is the part
homeowners are least warned about.

What not to do **Do not throw out the mattress or furniture.** It is the most expensive
instinct people have. Dragging an infested mattress down a hallway and a
stairwell distributes the problem across the building, and you will have bought a
replacement into a room that is still infested. Encasements after treatment cost
a fraction of new furniture and let you keep what you have.

Apartments, HOAs and rentals In multifamily buildings the unit boundary is a legal concept, not a physical
one. Bed bugs move between apartments through wall voids, shared plumbing runs
and electrical chases, and the single most common reason a multifamily bed bug
job fails is treating the complaining unit while the ones on either side and
above and below go untouched.

Treatment, and what to expect afterward We match the method to the situation rather than selling one approach for every
job — the room, the furniture, the extent and the building type all change what
makes sense. What is consistent is that treatment is targeted at harborage
rather than broadcast across surfaces, and that follow-up is planned from the
start.

Are they dangerous? Worth answering directly, because the anxiety around this pest is often worse
than the infestation.

Hospitality, short-term rentals and senior living Commercial bed bug work runs on a different logic from residential, because the
cost of a missed unit is a review, a complaint or a regulatory conversation
rather than an inconvenience.

Why we do not sell one method for every job There is a lot of marketing in this trade built around a single technique, and
we would rather explain our position than pretend the question does not exist.
If you travel Ten minutes of habit prevents most of what we treat in January.

Related work If the insects turn out to be bat bugs, the fix is
a bat specialist rather than bedroom treatment — bat bugs follow the colony, and we do not do bat work. If they
turn out to be fleas, that is [flea control](/services/flea-control/) and the
approach is different again. For property managers running multiple buildings,
our [commercial programs](/commercial/) cover inspection cycles and

title: Bed Bugs After a Trip — What to Do First
sections:
The window that matters Bed bugs move by being carried. They do not fly, they do not travel far on their
own, and essentially every residential introduction arrives in something
somebody brought into the building — most often luggage, occasionally
second-hand furniture, sometimes a bag that spent a night somewhere else.

What to do with the luggage tonight The principle is simple: do not let the bags into a bedroom until they have been
dealt with.

What to look for over the following weeks If something did come home with you, the evidence appears in a fairly consistent
sequence and mostly on the bed.

Where to look Bed bugs stay close to where people sleep, and their harborage preferences are
narrow and predictable.
What the timeline looks like Patience is required here, and it is worth knowing why.

Things that get mistaken for them A good share of the calls we take after a trip turn out to be something else,
and it is worth knowing the usual candidates before anybody panics.

Why we charge to verify Every other assessment we do is free. Bed bug verification is not, and it is
worth explaining rather than burying.
If nothing is found This is a common and legitimate outcome, and it is worth saying what it means.

If something is found Then the good news is that you have found it early, and early is worth a great
deal in this particular problem.

Reducing the risk next time None of this requires traveling anxiously, and a couple of habits do most of
the work.

What not to do while you are worrying The instinct to act decisively is strong here, and several of the obvious
actions make the situation measurably worse.

Second-hand furniture, briefly Since it is the other main route in: any upholstered item, mattress, bed frame or
piece of soft furniture acquired second-hand deserves a proper look before it
comes into the house. Seams, joints, undersides, bolt holes and the underside of
drawers.

Monitoring while you wait If you want more than a visual check over the following weeks, there are two
things worth doing and one worth skipping.

A word about how this feels We deal with this problem often enough to say something that is not really about
insects.

What we do We will search properly, tell you plainly what is and is not there, and quote
only what the finding supports.

title: Bed Bugs in a Student Rental
sections:
Two things make this different Bed bugs behave the same way everywhere. What changes in a student rental is the
context around them, and it changes the outcome more than the biology does.
Why September Bellingham has a pronounced bed bug season and it is not driven by weather.

Confirming it before anybody argues about it In shared housing there is real value in establishing whether this is actually
bed bugs before the conversation about money starts, because a large share of
suspected cases are something else.
Treating one room in a shared house We are asked this constantly and the honest answer is usually no.

The responsibility question We are a pest control company and not attorneys, so we will describe how these
situations usually work rather than tell you what your rights are. For an actual
determination on a lease or a dispute, Washington has tenant advice services and
the university has housing resources, and either is a better source than us.

What housemates actually have to do Preparation is where shared housing treatments fail, and it fails because it
only takes one person not doing it.
What you can do cheaply that genuinely helps On a student budget, three things are worth the money.
What treatment actually looks like For a shared house, the shape is fairly consistent.

Moving out with an infestation This comes up every June and it deserves a direct answer, because the wrong
handling turns one household's problem into three.

Storage units and summers away The other seasonal pattern worth knowing about is what happens to belongings
between June and September.

If you are the landlord A short note, because a fair proportion of the people reading this will be on
that side.
The older housing stock here Bellingham's rental housing has a character that matters for this problem.

Living with it while it is being dealt with Between the first visit and the last follow-up there are usually several weeks,
and people want to know how to get through them.

What we do We search properly, tell you what is actually there, and recommend a scope that
follows the building rather than the complaint.

title: Bites But No Bugs Found — What Next
sections:
A common and genuinely difficult situation Marks are appearing overnight. They itch. They look like bites. And the bed, the
mattress, the frame and the room have been gone over repeatedly with nothing to
show for it.

Why bites alone are weak evidence This is the part that surprises people most, so it is worth setting out
carefully.

What a proper search establishes The reason a negative search carries weight for bed bugs in particular is that
bed bugs are poor at hiding their evidence even when they are good at hiding
themselves.

Other things that bite at night If it is an insect, these are the realistic candidates and each leaves its own
signature.

Things that mark skin without biting This is the category people rarely consider, and it accounts for a good share of
the situations where nothing is found.
What to gather before the visit A few things make the search far more productive, and all of them are free.

What if there are pets Pets change the picture enough to be worth a section, and they are the most
commonly missed explanation in this situation.

Why we will not treat on suspicion We get asked to "just treat it to be safe" fairly often, and we decline. Here is
the reasoning.

What a negative result is worth People occasionally feel they have paid for nothing when a search finds nothing.
We would put it differently.

What we do when the first search is clear If nothing is found and the marks continue, there are sensible further steps and
we will talk them through rather than leaving it there.

The nest-mite scenario in more detail Of all the explanations on this page, this is the one most often missed, and
where the nest belongs to a rodent it is the one we are genuinely the right
people to call about, so it is worth expanding.

Which nest, and whose job it is The two animals produce the same experience in a bedroom and they do not produce
the same answer about who to call, so the distinction is worth drawing before
anybody books anything.
Being straightforward about this One last thing, said with care.

What happens when you call Tell us what you are seeing, where on the body, when it started, whether anyone
else in the household is affected, whether there are pets, and whether there has
been any noise, droppings or activity in the structure.

title: Bee Removal & Relocation in Bellingham, WA
sections: Start here: it is probably not bees Most calls we receive about bees are about yellowjackets.
Why we will not kill honey bees This is a firm position and worth explaining rather than just asserting.

Swarms A swarm is a colony in transit — a queen and a large cluster of workers that have
left a hive to establish a new one. They gather on a branch, fence post, wall or
vehicle in a dense mass, sometimes thousands of bees, while scouts look for a
permanent cavity.
Established colonies in a structure A different proposition entirely, and the reason this page exists.
Bumble bees Our default recommendation is to leave them, and here is why that is not laziness.
Mason bees, mining bees and the harmless ones Every spring we get calls about these, and they need no service at all.

Wood-boring bees The other genuine bee-related structural issue, and it belongs on a different
page.

What we actually do on a bee call **Identify, free of charge.** Species and situation. A large share of these calls
end here with advice.

Around the county **The agricultural corridor** — Lynden, Everson, Nooksack, Sumas. Managed hives
are part of the working landscape and berry pollination depends on them.
Identification matters more here than anywhere, because destroying somebody's
production colony is a genuine problem rather than an abstraction.
What it costs Identification is free and frequently the whole interaction.

Preventing a colony from moving in Scouts look for a dry, enclosed cavity of the right volume with a small defensible
entrance. Buildings offer plenty, and the ones that get colonies tend to get them
repeatedly.
If someone in the household is allergic This changes the calculus and it is worth saying separately.
Bees on the ground in autumn A common call that needs no service.

Why we take this position at all It would be easier commercially to treat every stinging-insect call the same way.
A wall colony sprayed is a quick job at a good margin, and most customers would
never know the difference until the honey came through the ceiling a year later.

What we need to know when you call **A photograph if at all possible.** It resolves the identification faster than
any description, and identification decides everything else.
Bees and pesticide use generally One more thing worth stating, because it applies to work well beyond this page.

Related work Most calls that start here end at
[wasp and hornet control](/services/wasp-control/). Structural holes from
wood-boring bees are
[wood-boring bee and beetle control](/services/carpenter-bee-control/). Closing a
cavity after a colony has been removed, and preventing the next one, is
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/).

title: Carpet Beetle & Pantry Pest Control | Bellingham WA
sections:
Two problems on one page The service covers two groups of insects that have nothing in common except that
both are source problems and both get treated wrong.

Carpet beetles: the larvae are the problem **Adults** are small, rounded, and often patterned in mottled white, brown and
black — the varied carpet beetle is the common one here. They feed on pollen and
nectar outdoors, they are harmless, and they are attracted to light. That is why
you find them on windowsills and in light fittings.

The source nobody finds If there is a carpet beetle problem and no obvious wool, the source is almost
always something dead.
Carpet beetle or clothes moth? The damage looks similar and the treatments differ, so the distinction matters.

The rash that is not bites Worth its own note, because it causes real distress and gets misdiagnosed
routinely.
Pantry beetles Different insects, same logic: find the package.

Why we do not spray a pantry Because the answer is removal, and product does not belong on food surfaces
anyway.

Around the county **Older city housing** — the Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York and
South Hill. Wool rugs and carpet in houses with a century of accumulated lint
under baseboards, plus soffits and eaves that have hosted bird nests for decades.
The highest carpet beetle volume in the county, and the cases where the source is
a nest rather than a rug.

What it costs Quoted from the visit, and usually modest, because these are localized problems
rather than structural ones.

How we work a carpet beetle job **Confirm what it is.** Bristly larvae and cast skins, or webbing. The difference
sends the job in two directions.

Preventing both **For fabric pests:** clean wool and natural fibers before storing, keep stored
textiles in sealed containers rather than cardboard, vacuum under and behind
furniture that rarely moves, and deal with pet hair and lint accumulation along
baseboards and in vents. Where a wool rug sits under a heavy piece of furniture,
lifting and vacuuming it once a year is worth more than any produc

Wood-boring beetles are a different page Worth separating clearly, because "beetle in the house" covers two unrelated
situations and only one of them is on this page.

Timing and life cycle Both groups have long, temperature-dependent development, and that shapes what to
expect.

Commercial and institutional Both groups turn up in specific commercial settings, and the answer is almost
always monitoring plus stock and storage discipline rather than application.

Before you call **Keep a specimen.** A beetle or larva in a small sealed bag, or a clear
photograph next to something for scale, settles the identification immediately.

Related work If there is webbing, you want [moth control](/services/moth-control/). If the source is a nest, it has to come out before treatment means anything; see [rodent control](/services/rodent-control/) where it is a rodent. If a rash is being read as bites, see
[bed bug control](/services/bed-bug-control/) for what genuine bed bug evidence
looks like. And the reason we will not treat overwi

title: Wood-Boring Bee & Beetle Control | Bellingham WA
sections: Two different problems, and hole size separates them Everything on this page starts with measuring a hole.

Carpenter bees **What they look like.** Large, roughly bumble bee sized, but with a **shiny,
hairless black abdomen** — that is the distinguishing feature. Bumble bees are
fuzzy all over. Carpenter bees have a densely haired thorax and a bare, glossy
rear.

Wood-boring beetles, which are the local one If you own an older home in this county with a damp crawlspace, this is the
wood-boring insect you are most likely to actually encounter.
Active or old? The most useful diagnostic on the page, and one that saves people money.
How we work it **Identify and measure.** Hole diameter, frass texture, location and timber type.
Sealing carpenter bee holes, in the right order Worth its own note because people reliably get this backwards.

Around the county **Decks and outbuildings everywhere.** Carpenter bee damage tracks unfinished
softwood rather than neighborhood, so it turns up wherever there are weathered
deck rails, fence posts and barn timber — which in this county is most rural and
lakeside property.
What it costs Quoted from the visit, and the two problems price very differently.
What we will not do **Treat inactive damage.** Old exit holes in dry timber need no product.

Telling wood damage apart Four different insects leave marks in structural timber and they are routinely
confused. The distinctions are practical rather than academic, because they send
the job in four directions.

Timing **Carpenter bees.** Adults emerge in spring and females begin excavating and
provisioning. The nuisance is most visible in late spring and early summer, when
males are hovering. The right time to treat, fill and finish is late summer or
autumn, after the current generation has emerged, which is why we often book this
work months after the call.

Preventing carpenter bee damage Almost entirely a finishing question, and it is one of the few pest problems where
ordinary property maintenance is the whole answer.

What we find in a crawlspace, and what it means Because most of our wood-boring beetle work happens under floors, it is worth
describing what an assessment actually looks at.

Buying or selling a property Wood-boring insect damage turns up in property transactions more than any other
pest on this site, and it is worth knowing how to read it.

Related work Anobiid beetle findings almost always lead to
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/) and
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/). The same moisture
supports [dampwood termites](/services/termite-control/) and
[moisture ants](/services/ant-control/), so these are frequently found together.
If the large bee at your deck turns out to be

title: Centipede & Millipede Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
Two very different animals, one message Both of these turn up for the same underlying reason, and both are worth reading
as information rather than as an infestation.

House centipedes, which are on your side The one that generates most of the calls, and the one where the honest advice is
hardest to hear.
Millipedes, and the autumn migrations The other common call, and it usually arrives all at once.
Garden and soil centipedes Worth mentioning because they get lumped in and they are not the same animal.
What actually resolves both The same list, because the driver is the same.
Why we usually recommend leaving centipedes alone Stated plainly because it costs us work.

Around the county **Older housing with damp crawlspaces** — Columbia, Sunnyland, York, Roosevelt and
the Lettered Streets. Post-and-pier foundations, unsealed crawlspaces and original
bathroom ventilation give both animals a continuous reservoir directly beneath the
living space. The highest volume of house centipede calls in the county.
What it costs Quoted from the property, and usually modest.
What you can do **Vacuum rather than crush**, particularly millipedes, which can stain.

What people try that does not help **Interior spraying along baseboards.** Both animals are transient indoors. The
ones you treat were dying anyway, and it does nothing to the reservoir.
When it is genuinely worth treating Having spent this page recommending restraint, here is the other side.

Reading the building from the insect This is worth stating as a general principle, because it applies across most of
this site and centipedes and millipedes are the clearest example.

The seasonal shape **Winter and early spring.** Both are present but quiet, living in the damp voids
and soil. Occasional centipede sightings in bathrooms as they hunt.

If you would rather not kill them A note for the households — and there are plenty in this county — who would prefer
to relocate rather than treat.

What to tell us when you call **Which animal.** Fast with long legs, or slow and curling into a spiral. That
single detail sends the visit in different directions.

What it means for an older Bellingham home A short closing note, because these two animals are so strongly associated with a
specific housing type here.

Related work The reservoir is nearly always damp, so the durable fixes are
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/) and
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/). If centipedes are
present, look for [silverfish](/services/silverfish-control/), which are usually
what they are hunting. The same damp perimeter also produces
[earwigs, sowbugs and pillbug

title: Cockroach Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
The identification decides the job The cockroach that matters in Whatcom County is the German cockroach, and the
treatment only works if it is aimed at where that species actually lives.
Getting this wrong wastes months.

German cockroaches, and why they are difficult Three things make this species harder than most household insects, and they are
worth understanding because they explain everything about the treatment.
Why spraying makes it worse This is the single most useful thing on this page.

Where they actually live On a German cockroach job the treatment is placement, so knowing where they
harbor is the work.

Apartments, and the unit boundary problem The most common reason a German cockroach job fails is that the scope was one
apartment.

Sanitation, honestly There is a version of this conversation that is really about blame, and we would
rather not have it.

The health side Worth being accurate about, because this is one of the few household pests with a
genuinely well-documented health effect.

How we work a cockroach job **Identify.** Confirm what it is and where it is breeding. Everything downstream
depends on it.

Around the county **Student and multifamily housing** — Sehome, Happy Valley, the Western campus
edge, and the apartment stock along the Guide Meridian corridor. High turnover
plus shared walls is the classic German cockroach situation, and secondhand
furniture and appliances moving between units in June and September is a reliable
vector.

What it costs Quoted from the visit. A single-family home with a contained German cockroach
population caught early is a straightforward job over a few visits. A multi-unit
building with an established population across several apartments is a program
rather than a treatment, and the honest scope includes the neighbors.

Before we arrive **Stop spraying.** Repellent products scatter the population and interfere with
bait, and they make the job longer.

How long it actually takes Setting expectations, because this is a service where impatience causes people to
do counterproductive things.

Commercial and food handling For restaurants, groceries, care facilities and any business under a food safety
program, cockroaches are a compliance problem as much as a pest one.
What people get wrong Two mistakes account for most of the jobs that drag on.

The nymphs are the tell If you want to know whether you have a breeding population rather than a stray,
look for the small ones.

Related work For apartment buildings and food-handling businesses see
[commercial programs](/commercial/). If the insects you are finding are small,
fast and in a column rather than scattered, that is more likely
[ants](/services/ant-control/), and if they are small, dark and jumping, see
[fleas](/services/flea-control/).

title: Commercial Pest Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
What a commercial program actually is The distinction worth understanding before comparing quotes: a commercial pest
program is not the residential service performed more frequently. It is a
different product.

Integrated pest management, in practice The term gets used loosely, so here is what it actually means on a site rather
than in a brochure. The
[EPA's introduction to integrated pest management](https://www.epa.gov/ipm/introduction-integrated-pest-management)
sets out the same sequence we work to — identify the pest, watch the numbers, act
on the conditions, and reach for a product only when the si

The record, which is half the service **Device-level history, where an account takes the add-on.** Sensors on the
traps and stations report how many interactions each device recorded and when,
and a trap that fires notifies us so a technician can be sent out rather than
the device waiting for the next scheduled day. See
[remote rodent monitoring](/services/remote-rodent-monitoring/).

Where the pressure actually is Across sectors the same handful of points account for most commercial pest
problems, and most of them are structural rather than about cleanliness.

Regulated settings Some sectors carry specific requirements, and knowing them is part of the job
rather than an add-on.

Getting started **A walk of the site**, and for anything larger than a single storefront it takes
a while, because most of what matters is not where the activity is but where the
access is.

Which businesses we work with The vertical detail sits on our [commercial hub](/commercial/), which covers the
specific pressures for dairy and agriculture, berry and food processing, marinas
and the working waterfront, restaurants and food service, schools and childcare,
healthcare and senior living, retail and grocery, multifamily and HOAs, property
management, government and municipal buildings

Around the county **Downtown and Fairhaven.** Restaurants, bars, retail and offices in older
masonry buildings with shared walls, basements and service alleys. Drains,
deliveries and waste handling dominate, and the buildings themselves supply plenty
of harborage.

What it costs Priced from the site rather than from a table, because the variables are real:
square footage, sector, how many exterior doors and docks, the number of devices
the site warrants, service frequency, and how much documentation your sector
requires.

What we ask of you A commercial program is a shared job, and being explicit about the split saves
argument later.

Staff training Frequently the highest-return part of a commercial program, and the part most
often left out.

Reporting and communication The part that determines whether a program is useful to you or just happening
around you.

What we will tell you that others may not **When the frequency is too high.** If a site is quiet across every device for a
sustained period, we would rather reduce the schedule than keep billing it. That
is a genuinely uncomfortable conversation in this industry and it is the right
one.

Getting a program started quickly For a site with an active problem rather than a preventive need, the sequence
compresses.

Small businesses, not just large ones Worth saying plainly, because commercial pest control is often presented as
something for facilities with a compliance department.

Related work The vertical-by-vertical detail is on the
[commercial hub](/commercial/). The structural half of most commercial programs is
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/). The recurring species
work sits on [rodent control](/services/rodent-control/), [cockroach control](/services/cockroach-control/) and
[fly control](/services/fly-control/). For homes rather than business

title: Crawlspace Cleanout & Restoration in Bellingham
sections:
What is actually under most houses here Crawlspaces in this county are wetter than almost anywhere else in the
continental United States, and a great many of them have never been properly
finished.
When restoration is warranted Not every crawlspace needs this work, and we would rather say so than sell it.
The order matters more than anything This is the single most important thing on this page.

The health side, stated plainly Rodent droppings and urine carry pathogens, and dried material becomes airborne
when it is disturbed. That is the whole reason this work has a method rather
than being a matter of a shovel and a bin bag.

What you get beyond pest control A meaningful part of the value here has nothing to do with insects, and it is
worth counting when you are deciding whether the job is worth it.

Vapor barrier or full encapsulation? Worth being straight about, because encapsulation is heavily marketed and is
frequently more system than a Whatcom County house needs.

What we do, what we hand off, and to whom We are a small local company. Being straight about the limits of that is more
useful to you than pretending there are none.

Around the county **Older Bellingham, above all.** The Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York and South Hill stock. Post-and-pier, low clearance, bare soil or a barrier from another
era, and a century of gutter history. The highest concentration of this work in
the county, and often the only real fix for a recurring insect problem upstairs.

What comes out, and where it goes Worth describing, because "cleanout" is vague and people reasonably want to know
what is actually happening under their floor.
The photographs We document a crawlspace before, during and after, and you get the images.
What it costs Quoted from the site visit, and driven mostly by three things.

Timing Late summer and early autumn is the best window, for the same reason it is the
right time for [exclusion](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/): it gets ahead of
the rodent push that comes with the September and October rain, and the space is
at its driest.
Attics, which are the same job upside down Everything above applies to attics with three differences worth knowing.
Rentals, sales and property management Two situations where this work carries weight beyond the pest problem.

Questions worth asking any company If you are getting more than one quote for this work — and you should — these
are the questions that separate them, whoever you end up hiring.

After the work A restored crawlspace does not need attention often, but it is worth knowing what
to keep an eye on.

Related work This work almost always follows [rodent control](/services/rodent-control/) and
runs alongside [exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/). Where
the attic is also involved, that is
[attic insulation removal and replacement](/services/attic-insulation/). And
where the moisture has been running long enough to bring in wood-destroying
insects, see [termites and wood-destro

title: Earwig & Sowbug Control in Bellingham, WA
sections: They live outside, and that is the whole point Earwigs are outdoor animals that occasionally end up indoors by accident.

What they actually are **European earwig.** Introduced, long established, and the dominant species in
this region — reddish-brown, flattened, with the distinctive forceps at the rear.
Males have curved pincers, females straighter ones.

Where they live, in the first three feet Almost every earwig problem is a perimeter problem, and the population is in a
narrow band around the building.
How they get in They are following moisture and dark, and they are small and flat.
The garden question Worth being even-handed about, because earwigs are genuinely both.

What actually works **Pull the mulch back.** A clear, dry band of six inches to a foot between mulch
or soil and the siding removes the habitat immediately against the building. This
is the highest-value change on most properties and it costs nothing but an
afternoon.
Why we do not spray indoors for these Because the insects indoors are already dying.

Around the county **Gardened city neighborhoods** — Columbia, Sunnyland, York, Roosevelt, Cornwall
Park, Happy Valley. Mature planting, deep mulch beds against foundations, and
older homes with worn door sweeps and unscreened crawlspace vents. The highest
volume of these calls.

What it costs Quoted from the property and generally modest, because it is perimeter work rather
than structural.

The year in earwigs **Late winter.** Overwintered females are underground in nest chambers tending
eggs. Nothing is visible above ground and nobody calls.
Sowbugs and pillbugs, specifically They get their own note because the reassurance is different.

Why the mulch matters so much Worth expanding, because it is the single most actionable thing on this page and
because the advice runs against standard landscaping practice.

Commercial and multifamily Earwigs come up in specific commercial contexts and the answer is the same
perimeter logic at a different scale.

What we will and will not sell you **We will** do perimeter and harborage treatment where the population is genuinely
heavy, close the entry routes, deal with a damp crawlspace that is acting as
habitat, and set up a spring perimeter program for a property where the
landscaping cannot practically change.

What to do before we come **Note which rooms.** Bathrooms, laundry and kitchen means humidity is the driver.
A bedroom on an upper floor suggests something different and is worth mentioning.

Traps, and what they are good for Worth a short note because the internet is full of earwig trap advice and most of
it is aimed at the wrong problem.

Related work Because this is a moisture and perimeter problem, it overlaps with
[silverfish](/services/silverfish-control/) and
[centipedes and millipedes](/services/centipede-control/) — both of which live
in the same damp band around a building. The durable fixes are
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) and, where the
crawlspace is the reservoir,
[crawlspace cleanout and res

title: Pest Exclusion & Repairs in Bellingham, WA
sections:
The argument for doing this at all Nearly every page on this site ends up pointing here, and it is worth saying why
plainly, even though it is the opposite of how pest control is usually sold.

A quarter of an inch That is the number worth remembering. A house mouse gets through roughly a
quarter inch — about a pencil. Both species can also work a gap considerably
smaller than the body looks, because the skull is the limiting dimension and it
is flatter than people expect.

Where they actually get in On Whatcom County housing stock the same short list accounts for most of what we
find. This is roughly the order we check.

Materials, which is where most exclusion fails The difference between exclusion that lasts a decade and exclusion that lasts a
season is almost entirely material choice. This is the part homeowners and a fair
number of contractors get wrong.

The crawlspace On the housing stock in this county, the crawlspace is where most of this work
happens and where most of the value is.
One job, several problems solved This is the part that makes exclusion good value rather than merely effective.
What we do not do We are not general contractors and we will not pretend otherwise to keep a job.

Rentals and property management Because Bellingham's rental standard is explicit about the quarter-inch
threshold, exclusion is a compliance item here rather than just good practice.

Timing **August and early September is the window.** Rodents move indoors as the ground
saturates through late September and October, so sealing before the push means
sealing an empty structure. Sealing in November means sealing animals in, which
is why at that point exclusion has to follow trapping rather than lead it.

Around the county **Pre-1940 city stock.** Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York and Roosevelt.
Post-and-pier, failing vent screens, unsealed penetrations and siding close to
grade. The highest-yield exclusion work in the county, and often the whole
solution to a rodent problem.

What a job actually looks like **The walk.** Someone goes around the outside of the building slowly, then gets
into the crawlspace and the attic. That last part is not optional — the entries
and the evidence are inside those spaces, and a quote produced from a walk around
the outside is a guess. We come out of it with a mapped list of openings, their
sizes, what is behind each one, and the conditi
Why exclusion is undersold in this industry Worth naming, because it explains why you may not have been offered it before.

Vacant and seasonal properties A specific case worth calling out, because it is common around Birch Bay, Blaine,
Semiahmoo and the lake.

What it costs Quoted from the walk-through, because the range is genuinely wide and depends on
access more than anything else.

Related work Exclusion sits alongside [rodent control](/services/rodent-control/), which is
where most of it originates, and
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/) and
[attic insulation](/services/attic-insulation/) where contamination has gone far
enough. Sealing a wall after a
[wasp colony](/services/wasp-control/) is dead is part of that job rather than a
separ

title: Crawlspace Vent Screening
sections:
The single most common way in If we had to pick one defect that accounts for more rodent entries into
Whatcom County homes than any other, it would be a failed crawlspace vent
screen.

Why not just close them The intuitive response is to block the vents entirely, and it is a genuinely bad
idea in this climate.

What actually works as a material The specification matters more than the labor here, and most of the failures we
find are material choices rather than workmanship.
What does not work We spend a fair amount of time removing previous attempts, so here is the list.

The rest of the ground-level picture Vents are the headline and they are rarely the only opening, so a proper job
looks at the whole foundation line.
Sequence matters There is one rule that governs the order of this work and it is not negotiable.

What else the vents affect Rescreening does more than keep rodents out, which is worth knowing when
weighing the cost.
Automatic and foundation vents A note on the vents themselves, since people ask.

Doing it yourself This is well within reach of a competent homeowner and we will not pretend
otherwise.

How to tell whether yours have failed You can assess this yourself in about fifteen minutes with a flashlight and it is
worth doing before anybody quotes anything.

What it looks like when it has been used Once you know what to look for, an active entry point is fairly obvious, and
knowing helps you judge urgency.

Landscaping is half the problem A surprising share of failed and non-functioning vents are not failed at all.
They are buried.

What it costs and what it saves We will not put a figure on a page, because vent counts, access and condition
vary too much to be honest about it. What we can set out is the shape of the
decision.

What we do We walk the whole foundation line rather than the vents you have noticed — every
vent, the access hatch, every penetration, the garage, the skirting, the grade
and any junction between structures.

title: Sealing a Quarter-Inch Foundation Gap
sections:
Why a quarter of an inch The number gets repeated so often that it sounds like a slogan, so it is worth
explaining where it comes from.

Where the gaps are Every building has a set of these, and after enough of them the list stops
varying much.

Finding them Systematic beats intuitive, and this is genuinely something a homeowner can do
well.

What actually holds The material has to resist teeth. That is the whole specification and it rules
out most of what gets sold for this.

What does not hold **Silicone or acrylic sealant alone.** A weather material with no mechanical
resistance. Gone in a night.
The rule about sequence One thing governs the order of this work and it is worth stating plainly.
Ventilation is not a defect An important distinction, because people occasionally seal the wrong things.

Doing it yourself Most of this is within reach of a competent homeowner, and we would rather you
did it well than paid somebody to do it badly.

Why this beats a recurring plan We are a pest control company arguing for the work that reduces the need for
pest control, so it is worth setting out the reasoning.

A worked example: the pipe under the sink To make this concrete, here is the single most common opening in a house and how
it gets closed properly.

The gaps at height Ground-level work stops halfway if the roofline is open, and on a fair number of
buildings here the roofline is where the problem actually is.
When to do it Timing changes both the price and the result, so it is worth a paragraph.

What good work looks like afterwards Since most people cannot easily judge exclusion work once it is done, here is
what to look for.

What we do We walk the whole envelope — the full foundation line, every penetration, the
garage, the deck, the junctions between structures, and the roofline — rather
than the one gap you have noticed.

title: Flea Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
The pupal stage explains everything Almost every frustrating flea story comes down to one biological detail, and once
you know it the whole job makes sense.
Why the vacuum matters more than you would think This is the part homeowners can do that genuinely changes the outcome.

What you actually have **Cat flea.** Effectively all of it. Despite the name, the cat flea is the species
found on dogs, cats and wildlife alike across this region, and it is what we are
dealing with in nearly every residential job.

Where they come from **Pets are the obvious route**, and the pattern is that a pet picks up fleas
outdoors, the adults feed and lay, and the eggs fall off wherever the animal
spends time. Eggs are not sticky; they drop into carpet, bedding and floor
cracks. The pet is the delivery mechanism, the house is the nursery.
The pet side, which is not ours We treat structures. We do not treat animals, and we would be wrong to.

How we work a flea job **Confirm it is fleas.** Springtails and carpet beetle larvae are the common
false alarms, and neither responds to this treatment.
Preparation Before treatment, and it makes a real difference.

Around the county **Properties against the treeline.** Sudden Valley, Silver Beach, Edgemoor and
the Whatcom Falls margins produce the highest flea volume in the county, and the
highest share of cases where the source turns out to be an animal rather than a
pet. Deck voids and crawlspaces that host denning wildlife, plus dogs that spend
their time in cover, is the combination.

What it costs Quoted from the property, driven by square footage, how much carpet and
upholstery there is, and whether an animal source needs resolving first by somebody who does that work.

The seasonal pattern here Our climate keeps flea activity going longer than a colder region would, but
there is still a shape to the year.

What does not work Worth listing, because the flea aisle is full of products that sell well and
perform badly.

If there is no pet in the house Worth separating out, because it changes the job entirely and it is a case we see
often around the forest edge and in older housing.
