The life cycle, briefly Worth having the shape of it, because every decision on this page follows from it.

Fleas and your yard A short section, because most of the outdoor advice circulating on this subject is
wrong.

Landlords, tenants and vacant units Fleas come up more often in rentals than most pests, and the responsibility
question follows a predictable pattern.

Related work Where the source is an animal rather than a pet, the real job is removing that animal — [rodent control](/services/rodent-control/) if it is a rodent, a wildlife specialist if it is not — and closing the space is
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/). If what you are finding
is in a bed rather than around ankles, see
[bed bug control](/services/bed-bug-control/) —

title: Fly & Gnat Control in Bellingham, WA
sections: Every fly job is a source-finding job This is the whole page in one idea, so it goes first.

Cluster flies, the local exception If you get a large number of slow, dark, slightly hairy flies at upstairs windows
on the first warm day of winter, you have cluster flies, and almost everything
above does not apply.

What the other species tell you **Fruit flies.** Small, often red-eyed, hovering around kitchens and bars. The
source is fermenting material: overripe produce, spillage under an appliance,
recycling that has not been rinsed, a mop bucket, the residue in a drain, or the
bottom of a bin. Almost always within a few feet of where you see them.
Drains, and why bleach does not work The single most common wasted effort in fly control.

How we work a fly job **Identify the species.** It is the diagnostic, and it usually narrows the search
to one or two possibilities immediately.

Commercial fly work Different in emphasis rather than method, and this is where fly control earns its
keep.

Around the county **The agricultural corridor** — Lynden, Everson, Nooksack, Sumas. House flies and
stable flies around livestock, manure and feed, at volumes that are a working
condition rather than an infestation. Management here is about waste handling,
moisture and timing rather than about treating a house.
What it costs Quoted from the visit, and it varies more by cause than by species.

What you can do first **Identify roughly where they are.** Which room, which window, near which
appliance. Flies concentrate near their source, and that alone narrows it a long
way.

The fly year in Whatcom County **Late winter and early spring.** Cluster flies waking in wall voids on warm days
and appearing at upstairs windows. Nothing is breeding — this is last autumn's
population emerging on the wrong side of the glass. Vacuum and plan the sealing.
Fly identification, simply Without a microscope, size and behavior get you most of the way.
Sanitation that actually matters Not general tidiness — the specific things that produce flies.

Light traps, and where they belong Worth a note because they are frequently sold as a solution and are really a
monitoring tool.

Related work Cluster fly work is [exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) in
practice. Blow flies indoors usually mean
[rodent control](/services/rodent-control/) or
a carcass to locate, and a wildlife specialist to keep it from happening again. For
commercial kitchens see [commercial programs](/commercial/). And if the small
insects around your damp bathroom are jumping rather th

title: Cluster Flies in Upstairs Windows
sections:
What they are The flies at your upstairs windows in October, and again on the first mild day
in February, are almost certainly cluster flies, and they are a completely
different proposition from the flies most people picture.

Why your house Cluster flies overwinter in aggregations — the name is literal — and they select
sites by warmth and exposure.

Why they keep reappearing This is the part that frustrates people, and the mechanism is simple once
explained.

Telling them from the flies that matter Two other flies get confused with these and one of them is worth acting on
urgently.

Why timing decides everything There is one honest thing to say about cluster fly work and it is about the
calendar.

Sealing, and what to seal Exclusion is the durable half of this and it is worth doing regardless of when
you start.

The other overwintering insects Cluster flies rarely arrive alone. The same walls, the same weeks and the same
openings serve a small group of insects that all do the same thing, and a
building with one usually has several.

The dead fly problem This is the part that gets overlooked and it produces a second wave of calls in
spring.
What to do about the ones in the room now Practical, immediate, and unglamorous.
What a realistic outcome looks like We would rather set expectations than oversell this.

The rural and farm situation A large share of the worst cluster fly buildings in this county are on acreage,
and there are a few things worth saying about that.

Windows themselves, and why upstairs Since the complaint is nearly always about upstairs windows specifically, it is
worth explaining the geometry.

What we will not sell you **A winter interior treatment.** Product applied inside a house in January does
not reach insects dormant in a cavity, and it puts residue where people live for
no return.

A note on chimneys and unused flues One structural feature deserves a mention because it produces the most dramatic
version of this problem.

What we do We look at the elevations they are using, find the openings at height, check the
attic for accumulation and for the connections into your rooms, and identify
whether what you actually have is cluster flies or one of the flies that means
something else.

title: Fungus Gnats in Houseplants
sections:
Not really a pest problem Small dark flies drifting up when you water, sitting on the soil surface,
appearing at windows, and generally being present in a way they were not a month
ago. Fungus gnats are one of the most common indoor insect complaints there is
and one of the least serious.

What they are Adults are small — a few millimeters — dark gray or black, with long legs and
long antennae relative to their body, and a weak fluttering flight. They are
poor fliers, which is why they tend to stay near the plants rather than
distributing through a house, though they are drawn to windows and screens.
Do they damage plants Mostly no, with specific exceptions worth knowing.
The method that works In order of importance.

What does not work **Spraying the adults.** They live a week and die anyway. Killing the ones flying
around does nothing about the several hundred larvae in the pot, and it puts
insecticide on plants and surfaces indoors for no benefit.
Where they came from Almost always with new material rather than through a window.

When the plants are not the source A few situations produce the same small flies from somewhere structural, and
these are the ones where calling somebody makes sense.
The flies that are not fungus gnats Two lookalikes matter, and one of them is a real finding.

What we would actually come out for We are not going to pretend a windowsill of houseplants needs a professional, so
here is where it does.
A four-week plan If you want this as a schedule rather than a set of principles, here it is.

Why this is worse in winter here Households in this county often notice fungus gnats appearing between November
and March, and there are two reasons that have nothing to do with the plants
themselves.

Growing media and why some are worse Not all potting material behaves the same way, and the choice makes a
measurable difference to whether this recurs.
If you keep plants and pets One practical note, since a lot of the advice circulating online ignores it.

What we will tell you If you call about this, you will get the advice above and an honest assessment of
whether a visit is worth your money. Frequently it is not, and we will say so.

title: Year-Round Home Pest Protection Plan | Whatcom WA
sections:
Who this is actually for Most of this site argues against buying treatment you do not need, so it would be
strange to put up a recurring plan page that pretends everyone needs one. Here is
the honest version.

Who it is not for **One identifiable problem with a fixable cause.** A wasp nest under an eave. A
gap in the foundation letting rodents in. Ants tracking to one moisture source.
Fix the cause, treat once, and you are done. Selling a year of visits for a
problem a single afternoon resolves is the practice that has given this industry
its reputation.

What the plan actually does **Exterior perimeter treatment**, applied where it matters — foundation,
entry points, eaves, and the harborage around the structure — rather than
broadcast across surfaces for the sake of appearances.
What it does not cover Plainly, because a plan that claims to cover everything is not a real document.

Timed to what actually happens here Most recurring plans in this industry run on even quarters because quarters are
easy to bill. The pest calendar in Whatcom County is not evenly spaced, and the
schedule should follow the pests rather than the invoicing cycle.

How it works with the guarantee The plan and the [guarantee](/our-guarantee/) are the same commitment described
two ways.

No contract, and why The long-term contract is standard in this industry and its real function is
retention rather than service quality. A company confident in its work does not
need a termination penalty to keep customers.

What it costs Priced from the property rather than from a table, because the variables are
real: square footage, lot size and how much perimeter there is, what is adjacent
— forest edge, greenbelt, farmland or suburb — the pest history, and how much
exterior structure there is to service.

Around the county **Forest edge and lakeside** — Sudden Valley, Silver Beach, Edgemoor, Whatcom
Falls. Continuous pressure from land you do not control, and the clearest case
for ongoing service anywhere in the county.

Getting started A free inspection first. We look at the property, tell you what is actually
happening, and give you our read on whether a plan is the right purchase or
whether something else is.

What a visit actually looks like Worth setting expectations, because "quarterly service" means very different
things at different companies and some of it is a truck in a driveway for six
minutes.
Changing or pausing a plan Circumstances change and the plan should be able to follow.

Commercial and multifamily The residential plan described above is built for houses. Businesses and
multi-unit buildings need something structurally different, and we run those
separately rather than stretching a home plan to fit.

What we track between visits The part of a plan that is easy to overlook is the record, and over a couple of
years it becomes the most useful thing about it.

The honest comparison If you are weighing a plan against calling as things come up, the arithmetic is
worth doing rather than guessing at.

Getting the sequence right If you are starting from a live problem rather than from prevention, the order
that works is consistent.

Related work Most plans are preceded by [exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/),
and many are preceded by a specific job — [rodent control](/services/rodent-control/),
[ants](/services/ant-control/) or [wasps](/services/wasp-control/) — that
resolved the immediate problem. For businesses rather than homes, the equivalent
is our [commercial programs](/commercial/), which add mappe

title: Clothes Moth & Pantry Moth Control | Bellingham WA
sections: Two completely different problems The word "moth" covers two situations that share nothing except the insect order.

Clothes moths **The two species.** The webbing clothes moth is the common one, leaving silk
tubes and mats on the fabric. The casemaking clothes moth constructs a small
portable case it drags around and feeds from — finding those little cases attached
to a garment or a rug is unmistakable once seen.
Why they avoid light, and why that matters This is the single most useful diagnostic on this page.

The soiling point Worth understanding, because it explains the pattern people find baffling — one
ruined sweater beside five identical untouched ones.

What actually works on clothes moths **Find and clean the source.** Everything in the affected area gets inspected and
cleaned. Dry cleaning or a hot wash kills all stages on washable items.
Mothballs and cedar, honestly Both are widely trusted and both are widely misused.

Pantry moths **The Indianmeal moth** is effectively the only one that matters here. Distinctive
once you know it: the outer two-thirds of the forewing carries a reddish-brown
coppery luster and the inner third is pale gray, so the wing reads as two colors
meeting along a line. [UC IPM](https://ipm.ucanr.edu/pdf/pestnotes/pnclothesmoths.pdf) and Clemson Extension both describe the split at
those pr

Finding a pantry moth source **Check everything, including sealed-looking packages.** Larvae chew through paper
and thin plastic, and they exploit folded seams without chewing at all.

Around the county **Bellingham's older housing** — the Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York and South Hill. Wool rugs, cedar closets that stopped working decades ago, and stored
textiles in attics and basements. Clothes moth country.
What it costs Quoted from the visit, and generally modest, because both problems are localized.

Protecting a valuable collection Where the items at risk are genuinely valuable — heirloom textiles, antique rugs,
a wardrobe of good wool, taxidermy, historic garments — the approach shifts from
treatment to conservation, and the priorities change.

What we will not do **Spray your clothes or bedding.** Application belongs on structure — closet
framing, carpet edges, baseboard voids — not on things worn against skin.

The moths you can ignore Most moths that appear indoors here are neither of the two problems on this page,
and it is worth being able to dismiss them.

Around the seasons **Late winter and early spring.** Stored winter woolens come out and the damage
from the previous storage season is discovered. This is when most clothes moth
calls arrive — the damage happened months ago in a dark closet.

What it looks like when it is working Both problems have long enough cycles that people struggle to tell progress from
luck, so it is worth naming the markers.

Before you call **Look for webbing** and tell us whether you found any. It is the fastest way to
separate a clothes moth problem from a pantry one, and it changes what we bring.

Related work If you find bristly larvae and cast skins rather than webbing, that is
[carpet beetle](/services/beetle-control/) and the same fabric damage has a
different cause. If the moths are coming from a bird or rodent nest in the
structure — which happens, because those nests contain feathers and hair — that nest has to come out first — see
[rodent control](/services/rodent-control/). And if

title: Remote Rodent Monitoring for Businesses | Whatcom
sections:
What it is Remote monitoring is a sensor fitted to the rodent devices in a commercial
program. The stations and traps stay exactly where a technician decided they
should go; the sensor is what changes, and what it changes is how quickly
anyone finds out that a device did something.

What you get out of it **Interaction counts.** How many times each device recorded activity, by
device, rather than an impression of how the site is doing.

Why the alert comes to us and not to you This is a deliberate choice and it is worth explaining, because most of the
industry sells it the other way.

Where it earns its money Remote monitoring is worth most where a device being left unattended is
expensive or where the site is too large to read by walking it:

What a sensor does not do This matters more than the feature list, and we would rather say it here than
have you find out later.

How it goes on an account **At the walkthrough.** We look at what you run now, where the devices are,
and where a hub can sit so the far end of the site still reaches it. Skyhawk
puts the hub-to-sensor range past 500 feet, which is generous and is still a
number a long building, a yard fence line or a concrete basement can eat, so it
is better answered by walking it than by assuming it.

Around the county Most of this work is in the commercial corridors — Bellingham's industrial
areas and waterfront, the Guide Meridian, the Burlington and Mount Vernon
retail and distribution corridor, and the agricultural accounts in the Lynden
and Everson area, where the yard is the problem and the building is downstream
of it. For the dairy and berry operations in particular, device-level histor

Getting it on your program If you are already a commercial account, it is a conversation and a quote. If
you are not, the monitoring is not where to start: the program comes first,
because sensors on badly placed devices produce fast, precise, useless
information. We would rather walk the site, get the devices right, and add the
monitoring to something that already works.

title: Rodent & Mouse Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
The Whatcom County rodent year Ask most people why rats come indoors and they will say cold. That is half the
answer, and the missing half is the one that decides when the work should be
done.

What you actually have Correct identification changes the work, so it is worth being specific rather
than saying "rodents."

How they are getting in Every rodent job is really an exclusion job, and exclusion starts with knowing
where to look. On Whatcom County housing stock, the same short list accounts for
most of what we find.

Signs, and what each one tells you **Droppings.** The most informative evidence on the property. Size tells you
species. Location tells you travel routes and where to set. Condition tells you
timing — fresh droppings are dark and pliable, old ones are gray, dry and
crumble under pressure. A crawlspace with only old droppings is a different
situation from one with fresh, and it changes what we reco

How we work a rodent job On commercial accounts, the devices can carry sensors that count interactions
and time-stamp them, and that tell us when a trap has fired so somebody is sent
to service it. That is an add-on rather than part of a residential job — see
[remote rodent monitoring](/services/remote-rodent-monitoring/).

How we use rodenticide, and what we choose We run rodenticide programs where they are the right tool, and we are
deliberate about which products go into them. This is worth explaining, because
"do you use poison" is one of the first questions people ask and the honest
answer has more in it than yes or no.

The damage, and why waiting costs more **Wiring.** Rodents gnaw insulation off conductors. This is the risk that
justifies acting quickly, and it is not theoretical.

Health, stated plainly Rodent droppings and urine carry pathogens, and the sensible response is
straightforward handling precautions rather than alarm.
Which rodent, and where Two numbers worth having before the geography, both from our own call volume.

Around the county **Prewar Bellingham** — Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York, South Hill.
Post-and-pier foundations, failing vent screens, unsealed penetrations. Norway
rats in crawlspaces. Almost always an exclusion job.

Renting, or managing a rental Rodents are the pest that most often turns into an argument about who pays, and
in Bellingham that argument has a legal shape worth knowing before you have it.

Commercial rodent work Commercial accounts differ in what gets documented rather than what gets done.
Device placement is mapped so an auditor or inspector can see the layout without
taking anyone's word for it, every visit produces a record of findings and
actions, and the recommendations that sit on your side — a dock door that does
not seal, waste stored too close to the building, drainage keep

What it costs We quote from the inspection rather than a price list, because the range is
genuinely wide. A mouse problem confined to one part of a house with two entry
points is a small job. A 1920s farmhouse with rats through the crawlspace,
forty feet of failed vent screening, and insulation that needs removing and
replacing is not.

Keeping them out Trim vegetation and tree limbs back from the roof and walls. Keep bark mulch
and soil below the siding line. Store feed, seed and pet food in sealed
containers rather than bags. Deal with fallen fruit. Keep firewood off the
ground and away from the house. Manage standing water and get downspouts
discharging away from the foundation. Check vent screens once a year — spring is
a goo

Related work Rodent jobs frequently turn into
[exclusion and repair](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) work, and where
contamination is significant they extend into
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/) and
[attic insulation replacement](/services/attic-insulation/). If what you are
hearing overhead turns out to be larger than a rat, that is nuisance wildlife rat

title: Droppings in the Kitchen — What to Do
sections:
What you have actually found Opening a drawer or pulling out a toe-kick panel and finding a scatter of small
dark pellets is a specific kind of unpleasant, and the first reaction is
usually to clean it up immediately and think about it afterwards.

Reading the size The species question is answered almost entirely by size, and it matters because
the response differs.
Reading the age Freshness tells you whether this is happening now or happened once.
Reading the pattern Where they are is as informative as what they are.

Cleaning up without making it worse This part has a right and a wrong method, and the wrong method is the intuitive
one.
The food question The instinct to throw everything out is understandable and usually excessive.
Where they are coming from Here is the part that decides whether this recurs.
What we do about it The work has a fixed shape.

Things people try first, and how they go Almost everybody does something before they call, and it is worth saying which
of those things help.
What a small number of droppings really means We get asked this a great deal, usually hopefully, so here is the arithmetic.

Why it always seems to be autumn Kitchen droppings are a strongly seasonal complaint in Whatcom County, and the
curve is consistent year on year.

Commercial kitchens are a different matter If the room in question is a restaurant, a café, a bakery, a taproom kitchen or
any food premises, the calculation changes and it changes quickly.

What to do next If you have found droppings, leave a representative patch undisturbed if you
reasonably can, clean the rest by the method above, and get the dry goods into
sealed containers.

title: Rats in the Crawlspace — Whatcom County
sections:
Why the crawlspace and not somewhere else If you were a rat choosing accommodation in Whatcom County, you would pick the
crawlspace.

How you find out Very few people discover this by going down and looking. It usually announces
itself another way.
What they are doing down there Understanding the pattern makes the response make sense.

How they got in There is nearly always a specific answer, and in this county it is usually one
of five.

What is outside feeding it A crawlspace population is supported by something above ground, and it is worth
being blunt about the usual suspects.

Telling rats from mice under a floor The two need different responses, and the crawlspace usually makes the answer
obvious once you know what to look at.

What it does to the rest of the house People are usually more concerned about the crawlspace than about the building
above it, and it is worth reversing that emphasis for a moment.

Coops, feed and the neighboring-property problem Two things come up so often on properties in this county that they deserve their
own note.

The cleanup question, answered honestly This is where the industry has a reputation problem, so we will be direct about
where the line sits.
Doing it in the right order The sequence is not arbitrary and getting it wrong costs money.

Moisture, which is usually part of the story A crawlspace with a rat problem very often has a water problem too, and the two
reinforce each other.

Safety if you are going down yourself Plenty of people want to look before they call, which is reasonable. A few
points worth having first.

What it takes and how long For a typical single-family house here with an established but not extreme
crawlspace population, the shape of it is a few weeks: trapping running while
the exterior gets closed, activity dropping through the second and third week,
then a check to confirm.

Where to start Tell us what you have noticed and roughly where, and we will come and look
properly — the length of the crawlspace with a light, not a glance through the
hatch, plus the full exterior at ground level.

title: Rodents in the Attic Insulation
sections:
Why the insulation is the target An attic is not inherently attractive to a rodent. It is hot in summer, cold in
winter, exposed, and a long way from food.

What it costs you in heat This is the part that rarely gets explained properly, and it is usually the
larger number.

What is up there The realistic list for a Whatcom County attic is shorter than people fear, and
it includes one thing we do not handle.

How they get to the roof Attic entry is a roofline problem, and it comes down to a familiar set of
defects.

When the insulation has to come out We want to be plain about this, because attic insulation replacement is one of
the easiest things in this trade to oversell.

The order the work goes in **Animals out first.** Trapping in the attic and in the connected voids, on the
runs and at the entry points, in numbers, checked and adjusted. We do not use
bait inside the envelope: an animal that dies in a soffit or a wall top is a
second problem, and one that is genuinely difficult to reach in a roof.

The ceiling plane, which almost nobody seals There is a second boundary in this job that gets far less attention than the
roofline, and in an occupied house it matters just as much.

Damp attics make everything worse A wet roof space is a worse pest problem than a dry one, and in this climate wet
roof spaces are not rare.

What we will not sell you **A full insulation replacement for scattered droppings.** If the material is
dry, lofted and structurally intact, cleaning the affected area is the
proportionate response. We would rather do the smaller job and keep the
relationship.

Timing, and the case for doing it in summer Attic rodent activity in this county follows the same seasonal curve as
everything else — pressure rises from late September, peaks through the autumn
and stays elevated into the new year. Most calls come when the noise starts,
which is to say once the animals are already in.

Signs from below Most people never go into their attic, so the evidence usually arrives
indirectly.

What stored belongings tell you Most attics double as storage, and the boxes are often better evidence than the
insulation.

Safety, briefly If you are going up to look, the standard precautions matter more in an attic
than almost anywhere else, because the material is dry and the space is
unventilated.

What you get from us We will look at the attic properly rather than from the hatch where it is safe
to do so, walk the roofline from outside, and check the connected voids and the
crawlspace, because a surprising proportion of attic activity arrives from below
through an interior wall rather than over the roof.

title: Scratching in the Walls at Night — What It Is
sections:
The sound is information Almost every call that starts with scratching in a wall begins the same way: it
is dark, the house is quiet, somebody is lying in bed, and there is a small
persistent noise on the other side of the plaster.

When it happens Rodents are crepuscular and nocturnal, which in practice means two activity
peaks: shortly after dark and again in the hours before dawn.
Where in the wall Height matters more than people expect.

What the noise sounds like **Scratching and scrabbling.** Claws on framing or on the back of the drywall.
Generic to all rodents, and the most commonly reported.

Why the wall is a hallway, not a home Here is the thing most homeowners have backwards, and it changes what a sensible
response looks like.
What is actually in there In Whatcom County the realistic list is short.

Why it started now Rodent calls in this county are strongly seasonal, and the pattern is worth
knowing.

What not to do **Do not put poison into a wall cavity.** This is the single most common
self-inflicted problem we get called to fix. The animal dies where you cannot
reach it, and a decomposing rodent inside a closed cavity produces a smell that
lasts for weeks and attracts flies on top of it. Sometimes the only remedy is
opening the wall to find it. It is also worth knowing that the EPA's
[restri
What we actually do about it The work has three parts and they run in a deliberate order.
Two things you can check tonight Neither of these requires tools, and both make the visit shorter.

Why the houses here leak where they do Whatcom County housing has a few recurring weaknesses that account for a large
share of what we find, and knowing them helps you understand why we go where we
go.

What to expect on timing For a mouse situation in a reasonably sound building, the usual shape is a
couple of weeks: trapping running while the sealing work is done, activity
dropping off through it, then a quiet check afterwards.
A note on the noise itself People ask us fairly often whether they should be worried, or just annoyed.

Getting it looked at If you can tell us roughly when the noise happens, roughly where in the house it
is, and what it sounds like, we can usually tell you on the phone what we
expect to find and whether it is even our sort of job.

title: Silverfish Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
A humidity problem in an insect costume Everything about silverfish follows from one fact: they need moisture from the air
to survive.

What you are looking at **Silverfish.** Teardrop-shaped, tapering from head to tail, covered in silvery
scales, with two long antennae in front and three long bristles at the rear. They
move in a distinctive rapid wriggle. They prefer cool and damp.
Slow, and why that matters Silverfish are unusual among household insects in how slowly everything happens.

What they damage Not the house, and not you. What they eat is starch, and that turns out to include
things people care about.
Where they actually live The ones you see are a fraction, and they are not living where you find them.

How we work a silverfish job **Confirm the species.** Silverfish or firebrat, because it determines whether we
are looking at damp cool spaces or warm mechanical ones.
The moisture work, which is the real treatment If you do only one thing, do this.

Around the county **The prewar city stock.** Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York, Roosevelt and South Hill. Post-and-pier foundations, unsealed crawlspaces, original bathrooms
with poor or no ventilation, and in many houses, original wallpaper with starch
paste behind it. The highest concentration of silverfish work in the county, and
almost always a crawlspace story.
What it costs Quoted from the visit, and the shape of the number depends entirely on the cause.

What you can do **Run the bathroom fan longer** — during the shower and for a good while
afterwards. A timer switch makes this automatic.

Protecting what they damage Where the loss is books, papers or textiles, storage changes the outcome more than
treatment does.
The centipede connection Worth knowing, because it changes how people react to a second insect appearing.

Commercial and institutional Silverfish come up in specific commercial settings, almost always for the same
reason.

The seasonal pattern Less pronounced than most pests here, because the reservoir is indoors and largely
buffered from the weather. But there is a shape to it.
What a silverfish finding tells us about the house More than most pests, this one is worth reading as information.
Firebrats, briefly Worth their own note because the place to look is completely different.

Related work The real work is usually
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/) and
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/). The same moisture
supports [moisture ants](/services/ant-control/) and
[dampwood termites and wood-boring beetles](/services/termite-control/), so a
silverfish finding frequently comes with company. If your damage is to wool,

title: Spider Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
The correction that most of this industry gets wrong Start here, because it is the single most useful thing on this page and because
the pest control trade has spent two decades getting it wrong in a direction that
happens to sell treatments.

What you actually have **Giant house spider.** This is the big one. Large-bodied, long-legged, brown,
and the spider that produces the majority of "there is an enormous spider in my
bathtub" calls in Whatcom County. It is a funnel-web weaver, it is harmless to
people, and it is very likely the spider you are looking at right now if you came
to this page in September.

Why fall is spider season Every year, from roughly August through October, people in this county discover
large spiders indoors and conclude the spiders are coming in from the cold.

Why spraying does less than you would expect Worth being straight about, because it is why our approach leans on physical work
rather than product.

Around the county **Older Bellingham** — Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York, South Hill.
Unsealed crawlspaces, original single-glazed windows and a century of settlement
gaps make for a lot of interior harborage. Cellar spiders in the crawlspace,
giant house spiders in the living space.

The spider year here **February through April.** Egg sacs laid the previous year hatch and spiderlings
disperse. Almost nobody notices, and it is the cheapest point in the year to
intervene, because removing egg sacs in late winter prevents a population rather
than reducing one.

Bites, and being straight about them Spider bites are massively over-diagnosed, in Washington and everywhere else.
Studies that follow up on presumed spider bites consistently find that most turn
out to be something else — commonly bacterial skin infections, which can look
strikingly similar and are considerably more common than a spider that bit
someone in their sleep.

When it genuinely is worth treating We have spent most of this page talking you out of unnecessary work, so here is
the other side.

How we work a spider job Identify what is actually present, and say so honestly. Remove webbing and egg
sacs from eaves, entries, corners, porches and outbuildings. Assess and reduce
the insect prey base, including the lighting question. Apply targeted exterior
treatment at entry points, foundation and eaves, timed for when it matters.
Recommend the exclusion work that closes the gaps for good. An

What it costs Spider work is quoted from the property, and the number tracks how much physical
work is involved rather than how much product goes on.
What to do with the one in your bathtub The practical question people actually have in September.

Spiders in crawlspaces, garages and outbuildings Most of the spider volume on any Whatcom County property is in the spaces people
do not spend time in, and that is where the useful work usually happens.

Related work Because spider numbers track their prey, a spider problem is often really an
insect problem — which is why this work frequently overlaps with
[fly control](/services/fly-control/) and general perimeter treatment. Sealing
the gaps that let spiders in is
[exclusion and repair](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) work, and it reduces
rodents and overwintering insects at the same time. If t

title: Is This a Hobo Spider?
sections:
The question behind the question Nobody really wants to know the species. What they want to know is whether the
large fast brown spider in the bathtub can hurt them, and whether they should be
worried about their children or their dog.

How the reputation was built and taken apart The hobo spider arrived in the Pacific Northwest from Europe some decades ago and
spread through the region. In the late 1980s a small body of work proposed that
its bite caused necrotic skin lesions — tissue death — similar to those
attributed to the brown recluse.

Why identification is genuinely hard We are frequently sent photographs and asked to confirm. We answer honestly,
which usually means saying it cannot be done from the image.

What you probably have In this region, the large brown spiders found in houses are most often one of
these.

The brown recluse question Because it comes up in nearly every conversation: brown recluse spiders do not
live in western Washington.

Reading the web instead of the spider If you want a practical way to narrow things down without catching anything, the
web is easier to identify than its occupant and it is right there in the corner.
Why so many in autumn The seasonal wave that drives most spider calls here has a simple explanation.

What actually reduces spiders indoors Spiders follow their food. A house with a lot of spiders has a lot of insects,
and dealing with the insects does more than dealing with the spiders.

Where they come in, specifically Since sealing is the measure that actually works, it helps to know the openings
that matter for spiders in this county's housing.
The case for leaving most of them alone We will make this argument even though it costs us work.

What the internet gets wrong about this A brief note on sources, because this is a topic where searching makes people
more frightened rather than better informed.

Where we do treat without hesitation **Black widows in a location people reach into.** A woodpile, a crawlspace, a
garage shelf, the underside of outdoor furniture, a shed used regularly. Worth
dealing with and worth being told about.

Catching one safely If you want a specimen identified, catching it intact is straightforward and does
not require touching anything.

What we will tell you Send a photograph or bring us a specimen and we will tell you what we think it
is, including when the honest answer is that it cannot be identified without
magnification.

title: Spiders Appearing Every Fall
sections:
It happens on a schedule There is a specific and consistent pattern to this, and once you see it as a
calendar event rather than an invasion it becomes considerably easier to live
with.

What it is not Several intuitive explanations for this are wrong, and they matter because they
lead to the wrong response.

Did they walk in, or were they already inside? The usual account of this — ours included, until we went back and checked it — is
that the spiders walked in from outside. There is a second account, from a source
that outranks most of what gets published on the subject, and the two belong side
by side rather than one instead of the other.
Which spiders The autumn walkers here are a fairly consistent cast.

Why the bathtub This gets asked more than anything else on the subject, so: they do not come up
the drain.
Why some rooms and not others The distribution inside a house is about routes rather than about preferences.
Why some years are worse The variation is real and it is predictable in hindsight.
The timing nobody uses Here is the practical point of this whole page.
What actually reduces it In rough order of how much difference each makes.

A month-by-month view If it helps to think of this as a yearly cycle rather than an annual surprise,
here is roughly how the spider year runs in this county.
Where treatment fits We do treat for this, and we will be clear about what it does.
What does not work There is a large market in autumn spider remedies and most of it does nothing.

Living with the season For most households the proportionate response is a small set of habits rather
than a program.

The other autumn arrivals Spiders are not the only thing walking in during those weeks, and it is worth
knowing what else the season brings because the calls tend to arrive together.
If somebody in the house is frightened of them We deal with this often and we would rather address it directly than skirt it.

What we will do We will walk the building, show you the specific openings the spiders are using
on your house rather than a generic list, and tell you which two or three
changes would make the largest difference.

title: Stink Bug & Overwintering Pest Control | Whatcom
sections:
One behavior, several insects Four different insects generate almost identical calls in this county every
autumn, and they all want the same thing.
What actually happens The sequence is the same every year and understanding it tells you when to act.
What they do not do Worth being explicit, because these calls come with more alarm than they warrant.

The odor, and why not to squash them Stink bugs earn the name. Disturbed or crushed, they release defensive compounds
that are strongly unpleasant and persistent, and on some surfaces the fluid
stains.

Why we will not treat inside the walls This is the most important thing on the page from a service standpoint, and it is
a case where the obvious-sounding solution is the wrong one.

The treatment that does work, and when **Exterior application in late summer**, applied to the elevations they gather on
before they arrive, does reduce how many get in. Timing is everything — it has to
be in place before the aggregation starts, which in this county means late August
into September. The same application in November is treating a wall the insects
have already passed through.
Brown marmorated stink bug, specifically Worth separating out because it is the one with a story beyond nuisance.

Around the county **Newer construction on open ground** — Barkley, Cordata, King Mountain, and the
newer stock around Ferndale and Lynden. Large unshaded south and west elevations
are exactly what these insects locate, and modern housing frequently has more
uninterrupted sunlit wall than older stock. The sealing is straightforward because
the detailing is better.

What it costs Quoted from the property, and priced as what it actually is: an exterior treatment
plus sealing, scaled to how much wall and how many gaps.
What you can do **Vacuum rather than crush**, and empty it outside.

Telling them apart Four insects, one behavior, and the identification only matters for the odor and
for the agricultural question.
Why the same house every year Because nothing about the building changed.

The overwintering calendar **August.** The window opens. Nothing has gathered yet, the weather is workable,
and this is when exterior treatment and sealing both do their most good. If a
house had a problem last winter, this is the month to act on it.

What people try that does not work **Bug bombs and foggers.** They do not reach wall voids, which is where the
population is. What they do reach is the living space, which is where the
population is not. And on the rare occasion they do kill an aggregation in a
cavity, that produces the dermestid problem described above.

If it is a rental Worth a note, because these calls come from tenants as often as owners and the
answer is usually structural.

Related work Cluster flies do the same thing on the same schedule and are handled on the
[fly control](/services/fly-control/) page. The sealing work is
[exclusion and repairs](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/), best done alongside
the [rodent-season](/services/rodent-control/) sealing in late summer. If what you
are finding is small, dark and damaging your carpets or clothing rather than just
sit

title: Bugs on the South Wall Every October
sections:
The annual gathering There is a particular week in most Octobers when somebody looks at the sunny side
of their house and finds it covered in insects.
Who is on your wall The cast is fairly consistent in this county.

Why your building Households often feel singled out, and the profile of an affected building is
fairly specific.

What happens next The wall clears, and a few weeks later they start appearing indoors, and this is
the part that confuses people.

The agricultural dimension Worth a paragraph in this county specifically, because brown marmorated stink
bugs are not only a household nuisance.

Timing is the whole thing There is one honest point to make about treating for this and it is about the
calendar.
Sealing, which is the durable half Exclusion works regardless of timing and it keeps working.

Dealing with the ones indoors **Vacuum them.** The most effective domestic method by a distance. They are slow
and easily collected.
The spring aftermath Two things follow in spring and it is worth knowing about both.
What a realistic result looks like We would rather set the expectation than oversell it.

Telling them apart in thirty seconds People send us photographs of these constantly, so here is a field guide short
enough to be useful while standing at a wall.

The vegetation question People frequently ask whether removing a tree would end it, and the answer is
usually no.

What we will not sell you **A winter interior treatment.** Product applied inside a house in January does
not reach insects dormant in a cavity, and it puts residue in living space for no
return.
A note on the smell Since it is the thing people ask about most with stink bugs, briefly.

What we do We look at the elevations they are actually using, find the openings above and
around them, check the attic for accumulation and for the routes into your
rooms, and identify which species you have — because a wall of boxelder bugs and
a wall of stink bugs point at different things nearby.

title: Termite & Wood-Destroying Pest Control in WA
sections:
What we actually have here Nearly everything written about termites online is about a different insect in a
different climate. Search the topic and you will get material about eastern
subterranean termites, Formosan termites, mud tubes, soil barriers and bait
station perimeters — an enormous industry built around species that are
genuinely destructive across the South and East.

The moisture point, which is the whole point A dampwood termite colony cannot establish in sound, dry lumber. It is not
capable of it. So when we find one in a structure, the finding is not really
"you have termites." The finding is **this wood has been wet for a long time.**

Telling termites from carpenter ants The two get confused constantly, especially during spring and fall swarms, and
the distinction changes the entire approach.

Swarming season **Dampwood termites swarm in late summer and fall**, roughly August through
October, on warm evenings. They are strongly drawn to lights, which is why the
classic report is a large winged insect at a porch light or a window in
September.

The insect nobody warns you about If you own an older home in this county with a damp crawlspace, the wood-boring
insect you are statistically most likely to encounter is not a termite at all.

How we work a wood-destroying pest job **Identify the insect.** Termite, carpenter ant, or wood-boring beetle. Everything
after this depends on it.

Around the county **Bellingham's oldest housing.** Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York and South Hill.
Post-and-pier foundations with sill plates close to grade, unsealed crawlspaces,
and a century of gutter and flashing history. The highest concentration of
dampwood and anobiid findings in the county.

What the damage looks like over time Dampwood termites work slowly compared to the subterranean species that generate
most of the industry's marketing, and anyone selling you urgency about an
imminent collapse is overselling.

What it costs Quoted from the site visit, and the range is wide because the variable is not
really the insect.

Prevention, which is just moisture control Keep gutters clear and downspouts discharging away from the foundation. Maintain
a working crawlspace vapor barrier and address standing water. Keep soil and bark
mulch below the siding line. Store firewood off the ground and away from the
structure. Remove stumps and buried wood where you reasonably can. Check deck
ledger flashing. Keep irrigation off th

Buying or selling a house here Worth addressing directly, because it is when most people first hear the word
termite in Whatcom County.

What we will not sell you Soil-barrier treatment for a dampwood infestation. The species has no soil
dependency, so treating the perimeter of a house for an insect living in a wet
window header is money spent on the wrong problem.

What we find in a crawlspace, in order of frequency Most of this work happens under floors, so it is worth describing what the space
actually tells us.

Timing Unlike wasps or rodents, this work has no urgent season — the damage accrues over
years rather than weeks, so there is no month where acting is dramatically better
than another.

Related work The same moisture that supports termites supports
[moisture ants](/services/ant-control/), and the two are found together
regularly. Correcting the conditions is usually
[crawlspace cleanout and restoration](/services/crawlspace-restoration/) and
[exclusion and repair](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) work. Where wood has
been damaged badly enough to need replacement, that is a carpe

title: Dampwood Termites in a Crawlspace
sections:
A moisture problem with an insect in it Dampwood termites are the termite of this region, and the single most important
thing to understand about them is that they are a consequence rather than a
cause.

What they are and what they look like Dampwood termites in the Pacific Northwest are notably large as termites go, and
they are most often encountered in one of three forms.

Where they turn up The list of locations in a Whatcom County crawlspace is short and consistent,
because it follows the water.

Reading the damage Termite work looks different from the other things that eat into timber here, and
the differences are visible without magnification.

What else is going on down there A crawlspace that has produced dampwood termites will almost always show the rest
of the damp-building picture, and it is worth looking at all of it at once.
What we can and cannot do We want to be exact about this because it affects who you need to call.
What treatment involves Assuming the identification is settled, the work has a defined shape.
Order of operations The sequence saves money, so it is worth stating plainly.

The other termite in this region Dampwood is the species most people here encounter, but it is not the only one,
and the distinction changes the work substantially.

What the swarm means Most households first learn about this from a swarm rather than from a
crawlspace, so it is worth explaining what that event is telling you.

When a sale is involved This finding shows up in transactions more than most, because a crawlspace is
exactly where a buyer's inspector looks and the sill plate is exactly what they
probe.

Prevention, which is mostly plumbing and drainage The measures that keep dampwood termites out of a building have almost nothing
to do with insects.

How urgent is it, honestly People understandably want to know whether their floor is about to fail, and the
proportionate answer sits between the two extremes people arrive with.

What we will not sell you **A treatment over an unrepaired leak.** It is the definition of a job that comes
back.

What we will do We will go under the building properly — the whole length with a light, not a
look from the hatch — and probe the structural timber rather than glancing at it.

title: Soft Wood Around a Window Sill
sections:
What a soft sill is telling you Somebody goes to repaint a window, or cleans a sill, or leans on one, and the
wood gives. Sometimes paint has bubbled. Sometimes a screwdriver goes in with
almost no resistance and comes out with damp fibrous material on it.

The probe test, done properly This is the most useful thing a homeowner can do before anybody comes out, and
it costs nothing.

Where the water is getting in At a window opening, the list is short and the same defects recur across the
county's housing.

Which insects, and what they mean Once wood is wet and softening, it becomes habitable for several things, and
each leaves a distinct signature.

How far it goes This is the question people most want answered and the one that most often
surprises them.

Why filler and paint make it worse The instinct to fill and repaint is strong, and it is worth explaining why it is
usually the wrong move.
What a real repair looks like For reference, since it will be somebody else doing it.

The signs that come before softness Decay announces itself for a while before a probe confirms it, and knowing the
early signals lets people catch this at the cheap stage.

Which windows in which houses The building stock in this county fails in patterns, and knowing yours helps
predict what you will find.

The condensation cases Worth a separate note because they are commonly misdiagnosed and the repair is
different.

When it comes up in a sale Soft exterior joinery is one of the most frequently flagged items in a property
transaction here, and it produces a predictable sequence.

Keeping the next one from happening Once a sill has been repaired properly, the maintenance that keeps it sound is
modest and almost nobody does it.

What we will do We will probe the sill and everything around it, work out where the water is
coming from, check whether anything is living in the timber, and look at the
structure below that elevation because the answer is frequently further down
than the finding.

title: Wasp & Hornet Control in Bellingham, WA
sections:
The late-summer problem Almost every wasp sting in Whatcom County happens in a six-week window, and
understanding why makes the whole season predictable.

What we actually have here **Bald-faced hornet.** Despite the name this is a yellowjacket, not a true
hornet. Large, black and ivory-white, and it builds the football-shaped gray
paper nest people photograph — hanging from a branch, a soffit, a shrub or
occasionally a wall. Genuinely defensive within several feet of the nest. This
is also the insect most often reported to us as a giant hornet.

About the northern giant hornet This deserves its own section here, because Whatcom County is where it actually
happened and the local memory of it is genuine.

Where the nest is decides the job **Ground nests.** Western yellowjacket, entrance often no bigger than a coin,
usually found by accident. Dangerous specifically because they are invisible and
because mowing or digging provokes a mass response. Treatment goes into the
entrance and the colony traffic does the rest, but it has to be done properly and
at the right time of day.

Safety, said plainly Wasps sting repeatedly — unlike honey bees they do not lose the sting — and a
disturbed colony will pursue. A yellowjacket ground nest hit by a lawnmower can
deliver dozens of stings in seconds.

What about bees? We do not kill honey bees, and we will tell you when what you have is bees rather
than wasps.

How we work a wasp job **Identify and locate.** Species and nest type change the method entirely, and a
surprising number of calls turn out to involve two nests rather than one. Where
the entrance is a gap in siding we want to know what is behind it before we
treat.

Around the county **Older Bellingham neighborhoods** — Lettered Streets, Columbia, Sunnyland, York,
Roosevelt. A century of siding, trim and utility penetrations means more cavity
entrances than newer stock, and German yellowjackets in wall voids are common.

Commercial wasp work Late-summer wasp pressure is a scheduling problem for commercial sites rather
than an emergency, and it is one of the few pest issues where the calendar is
predictable enough to plan around.

Reducing them next year The highest-value intervention is in **spring**, and almost nobody does it. In
April and May a founding queen is building alone, the nest is tiny, and the whole
colony is one insect. Knocking down small starter nests under eaves and in
sheltered corners at that stage prevents the September problem entirely, and it
carries almost no risk.

What it costs Wasp work is quoted from what the nest is and where it sits, and the range is
narrower than most of our services because the job is usually bounded.

What to do right now, if there is a nest If it is not in anyone's way, the honest answer is often to leave it. A
bald-faced hornet nest high in a tree at the back of a lot is doing no harm and
will be dead by December. Paper wasps under a shed eave are useful predators.

Related work Wasp jobs regularly reveal the gap that let the colony in, which is
[exclusion and repair](/services/exclusion-and-repairs/) work. If what you have
under the eaves turns out to be a wood-boring bee rather than a wasp, that is
[wood-boring bee and beetle control](/services/carpenter-bee-control/). And for
commercial sites — schools, food handling, marinas — late-summer wasp pressure is

title: Bald-Faced Hornet Nest in a Tree
sections:
The nest everyone recognizes Of all the stinging insect situations on a residential property, this is the one
that produces the most immediate alarm, and it is easy to see why. A mature
bald-faced hornet nest is a gray, layered, papery structure the size of a
football or larger, hanging visibly in a tree, a hedge, a shrub or occasionally
against a building.

What they actually are Despite the name, bald-faced hornets are not true hornets. They are a large
black and white species of yellowjacket, closely related to the ones that nest
in the ground, and their behavior sits between the two. UC IPM handles them
under [yellowjackets and other social wasps](https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7450.html)
rather than under hornets, for that reason.

The annual cycle, which decides everything Almost every practical question about these nests is answered by the life cycle,
so it is worth setting out clearly.

Why the leaf-fall discovery is usually a non-event The single most common version of this call goes like this: the leaves came down
in October, and there is an enormous hornet nest fifteen feet up in the maple
that nobody knew about.
When it genuinely should come out Position and timing decide it, not size.
How defensive are they, honestly Somewhere between the reputation and the reassurance.

What not to do **Do not knock it down.** A dislodged nest releases the whole colony at once, on
the ground, next to you. This is the classic way people end up with dozens of
stings.

What removal actually involves Where a nest genuinely needs treating, the work is straightforward for somebody
properly equipped and genuinely unwise for somebody who is not.

If somebody has been stung Most stings from this species are a local event and resolve on their own, but it
is worth knowing what normal looks like and what does not.

What we tend to find on a property When we come out for one nest, we look at the whole property, because these
rarely occur in isolation and the other findings change the advice.

Telling it apart from other nests **Paper wasps** build small, open, umbrella-shaped nests with visible cells and
no outer shell, usually under eaves, rails and in sheds. Much smaller colonies
and considerably less defensive.

Living alongside one For the nests that do not need removing, a few sensible measures make the rest of
the season straightforward.

Nests on buildings rather than in trees A proportion of these end up on a house rather than in a tree, and the
calculation shifts when they do.
Trees, pruning and next year Two practical points about the tree itself, since that is where the nest is.

What we will do We will look at it, tell you what it is, tell you how close it is to anything
that matters, and give you an honest recommendation — which is frequently that
it can stay.

title: Wasp Nest in a Wall Void
sections:
What you are looking at The usual description goes something like this: wasps are going in and out of a
small hole in the siding, under a soffit, at the corner of a window trim, beside
a dryer vent, or where a cable enters the wall. There is no nest visible. Just
traffic.

The one thing not to do We will put this before everything else because it is the mistake that turns a
manageable job into a bad afternoon.

Working out what is in there Before anything is treated, it is worth establishing which insect you have,
because the answers diverge sharply.

Reading the entrance The hole tells you things, and you can gather all of it from a safe distance on
a warm afternoon.
What treatment involves The approach that works is unglamorous and it is done from outside.
Whether the nest has to come out This is the question we get most and the answer is usually reassuring.

Why the wall in the first place If you want to reduce the chance of this recurring, it helps to know what a
founding queen is looking for in April.

What happens after the colony is gone There is a second act to a wall-void nest that nobody warns people about, and it
is worth knowing so it is not mistaken for a new problem.

Multi-unit buildings and rentals Wall voids in shared buildings raise a practical complication that a
single-family house does not.

Timing across the season An early-summer void nest is a small job. The colony is modest, the treatment is
straightforward, and the amount of material left in the wall afterwards is
negligible.

When it is inside a room Occasionally the first sign is not traffic outside but wasps appearing indoors —
one or two a day at a window, in a bedroom, in an upstairs hallway.

Staying safe while you wait Most void nests are dealt with within a few days of the call, and there are
sensible precautions for the interval.

What we will not sell you **A same-visit treat-and-seal.** Sealing before returning foragers have stopped
arriving is either premature or performed on a live colony, and neither is good
work.

What we do We identify the insect first, because honey bees and bumble bees do not get
treated and yellowjackets do.

title: Yellowjackets in the Lawn — Ground Nests
sections:
The nest you cannot see Every wasp situation on a residential property has its own character. A paper
wasp nest under an eave is visible, small and usually manageable. A hornet nest
in a tree is unmissable. A yellowjacket colony in the ground is neither, and
that is precisely what makes it the one we take most seriously.

Where the nests are Yellowjackets choose sites with a particular set of qualities, and once you know
them you can predict where a nest will be on most properties.

Reading the year The seasonal curve is the single most useful thing to understand about
yellowjackets, because it explains almost everything people notice.
Finding the entrance safely If you suspect a ground nest, the way to confirm it is to watch, not to look.

Why the home remedies are a bad idea There is a well-established folk repertoire for ground nests and every item in
it puts a person directly over an angry colony.

What removal involves Done properly, a ground nest is treated rather than excavated, and the equipment
matters more than the technique.

When leaving it alone is the right answer We will say this on site and we will say it here: not every ground nest needs
treating.
If a nest has already been disturbed This happens most often mid-mow, and the response matters.

Telling them apart from the things they get confused with Several insects nest in or near the ground here and only some of them are worth
treating, so identification is worth a moment.

Reducing the odds next year A few practical measures genuinely lower the number of ground nests on a
property.

Farms, acreage and working properties A ground nest on a working property is a different risk calculation from one in
a suburban back garden, and a good share of this county is working property.

Do the traps help? Hanging traps are the most common thing people buy for this, and the honest
answer is that they have a narrow use.

What we do We locate the nest properly, assess the access and the depth, and treat it with
the right equipment at the right time of day.

title: WDO Treatment for Home Sales | Whatcom County
sections:
Who this page is for You are buying or selling a house in Whatcom County. An inspector has been
through it and produced a document listing wood-destroying organisms, or
conditions conducive to them, and now somebody has to deal with it before the
sale closes.

The two roles, and why they are not the same company There are two distinct pieces of work in a transaction like this, they require
different credentials, and it genuinely matters which one you are asking for.

What our license actually covers Our people hold [Washington State Department of Agriculture](https://agr.wa.gov/services/licenses-permits-and-certificates/pesticide-license-and-recertification/pesticide-and-spi-licensing/commercial-applicators/structural-pest-inspectors) licenses — a
commercial applicator license, which under the state's Pesticide Application
Act attaches to the business of apply

The organisms, and what treatment actually involves Six things turn up on findings in this county with any regularity. They are
genuinely different problems and they need genuinely different work, which is
why a single flat "termite treatment" price is usually a sign that nobody has
looked properly.

Conducive conditions, which usually matter more than the insects Most findings in Whatcom County include a section on conditions conducive to
wood-destroying organisms, and in our experience that section is the one worth
reading twice.
How the timing works Transactions run on dates, so here is the realistic sequence.

For agents, lenders and escrow officers We work with a number of Whatcom County agents and we know what makes this easy
on your side.

What we will not do **We will not issue the report.** Repeating it because it is the thing people
most often hope we will bend on. We are not licensed for it.

What drives the cost We do not publish a flat figure for this work, because the variation is real and
a headline number would be misleading.
What the treatment visit itself looks like People are often surprised by how much of the day is spent not treating.

If you are the buyer, before the finding comes back There is a short list worth walking yourself, because it tells you what is
likely coming and it costs nothing.
